english: I rang him twice and it went straight to voicemail both times, so I just texted him instead.
grammar: 'Marqué' and 'mandó' are preterite – each call and each bounce to voicemail is a finished, counted event.

target: Cuando llegamos por primera vez, nos miraron con sospecha durante tres veranos seguidos.
english: When we first arrived, they eyed us with suspicion for three straight summers.
grammar: 'Durante tres veranos seguidos' is a closed, counted span – so 'nos miraron' sits in the preterite.

target: Perdí una tanda entera porque el horno se apagó a la mitad.
english: I lost a whole batch because the kiln cut out halfway through.
grammar: 'Perdí' and 'se apagó' – both preterite: two single completed events, the loss and the cut-out behind it.

target: Mi hijo y mi esposo la pasaron genial en su viaje.
english: My son and my husband had a great time together on their trip.
grammar: 'La pasaron genial' – Latin American 'pasar' takes a fixed 'la' for having a good time; the 'la' points at nothing.

target: En fin, el mantel quedó manchado y el vino se acabó, pero la cena estuvo estupenda.
english: Ah well, the tablecloth got stained and the wine ran out, but the dinner was lovely.
grammar: 'quedó', 'se acabó', 'estuvo' – three preterites, each event closed and ticked off one by one.

target: Hicimos judo en familia durante años: empezamos en Lyon y terminamos en Storrington.
english: We did judo as a family for years: we started in Lyon and finished up in Storrington.
grammar: Bookends call for the preterite: 'empezamos en Lyon y terminamos en Storrington' – both ends of the span closed.

target: En Lyon hacíamos judo toda la familia, hasta los más chicos.
english: In Lyon the whole family used to do judo, even the littlest ones.
grammar: Used-to habits sit in the imperfect: 'hacíamos judo' – a routine with no start or finish in sight.

target: En Pulborough, los mirlos y los petirrojos venían al jardín a la misma hora todas las tardes.
english: In Pulborough the blackbirds and robins would come to the garden at the same time every afternoon.
grammar: 'venían' – the imperfect for a past routine: they turned up daily, with no start or finish in the frame.

target: Desde ciertos ángulos, Scout se veía muy noble.
english: Scout looked very noble from certain angles.
grammar: 'Se veía' – 'verse' means to look a certain way, and the imperfect keeps it a standing impression.

target: Latour de France quedaba lejísimos en carro.
english: Latour de France was a very long drive away.
grammar: 'Quedaba lejísimos' – the imperfect suits where places sat in the past: a state, not an event.

target: De niña ni me acercaba a los caballos: me parecían enormes.
english: As a child I wouldn't even go near a horse: they seemed enormous to me.
grammar: Childhood scenes live in the imperfect: 'ni me acercaba' – a standing state back then, not one event.

target: Las leyendas chinas ya describían un caballo con un bigote fino y un corazón noble.
english: Chinese legends already described a horse with a fine moustache and a noble heart.
grammar: The imperfect leaves the past open-ended: 'ya describían' – the legends were already at it, with no endpoint.

target: De chicos lavábamos los platos por turnos, y nadie se salvaba.
english: As children we did the washing-up in turns – nobody got out of it.
grammar: 'De chicos lavábamos' – the imperfect handles childhood habits: washing-up that repeated, no single occasion.

target: Al principio quedaba agotada después de montar, ahora el cuerpo ya sabe lo que le toca.
english: At first I'd be worn out after riding, now my body knows what's coming.
grammar: The imperfect covers all the early rides at once: 'quedaba agotada' – how it went every time, no single event.

target: Nuestro primer carro era marrón, un color que ya casi no se ve en la calle.
english: Our first car was brown – a colour you hardly see on the road any more.
grammar: 'Era marrón' – past description takes the imperfect: the car's colour is a state it had, not an event that happened.

target: Antes yo nadaba solamente en verano, el resto del año ni se me ocurría meterme al mar.
english: I used to swim only in summer, the rest of the year it wouldn't even have occurred to me to get in the sea.
grammar: 'Antes' plus the imperfect is the used-to recipe: 'nadaba solamente en verano' – a habit with no end date.

target: En los setenta, Scout mediaba discretamente entre las grandes potencias.
english: In the seventies, Scout quietly mediated between the great powers.
grammar: 'Mediaba' is imperfect – the tense for what carried on through an era, no start or finish in view.

target: Al principio la carretera hasta Josselin me parecía eterna, ahora me la sé de memoria.
english: At first the road to Josselin felt endless, now I know it by heart.
grammar: 'Me parecía' is imperfect – past impressions have no start or finish, so seeming sits in the background tense.

target: De noche, cuando la casa por fin quedaba en silencio, avanzaba con las traducciones atrasadas.
english: At night, once the house had finally gone quiet, I'd get on with the translations I was behind on.
grammar: 'Quedaba' and 'avanzaba' – both imperfect because this is a routine that repeated night after night.

target: En esa época cualquier cosa me ponía de mal humor: el tráfico, el ruido, todo.
english: Back then anything would put me in a bad mood – the traffic, the noise, everything.
grammar: 'Me ponía de mal humor' – imperfect '-ía' spreads the mood over a whole era, no single incident in sight.

target: De niños, mis hijos se caían con una regularidad casi admirable.
english: As children, my sons fell over with almost admirable regularity.
grammar: 'Se caían' is the imperfect of habit – falling was the regular pattern back then, not one single event.

target: De niño, Pierre hacía muchísimas preguntas.
english: As a child, Pierre used to ask a lot of questions.
grammar: Spanish makes its questions: 'hacía muchísimas preguntas' – asking questions is 'hacer preguntas'.

target: Antes me daba pena equivocarme. Ahora me río y sigo conversando como si nada.
english: I used to be embarrassed about slipping up – now I just laugh and carry on talking as if nothing's happened.
grammar: 'Me daba pena' sits in the imperfect – a feeling that kept recurring back then, not a one-off.

target: Cuando era niña, los cumpleaños se festejaban en la casa y el pastel siempre era de vainilla.
english: When I was little, birthdays were celebrated at home and the cake was always vanilla.
grammar: 'Se festejaban' – the imperfect for how things routinely went back then, custom rather than one event.

target: Scout era una perra tontita con cierta debilidad por la caca.
english: Scout was a silly dog with a fondness for poo.
grammar: The '-ita' ending is affectionate: 'tontita' softens silly into endearingly silly.

target: La recepción del hotel tenía una luz tan apagada que apenas se podía leer el mapa.
english: The hotel reception had such dim lighting you could barely read the map.
grammar: 'Tenía una luz tan apagada' – background description of the past scene, so the imperfect rather than 'tuvo'.

target: Antes hacíamos el cruce de noche, pero ahora preferimos salir por la mañana.
english: We used to do the crossing overnight, but now we prefer to leave in the morning.
grammar: 'Antes hacíamos' – 'antes' + imperfect is the used-to formula, and 'ahora preferimos' swings back to the present.

target: Antes la gente se vestía elegante hasta para ir al banco, ahora vamos a todos lados en ropa cómoda.
english: People used to dress smartly even to go to the bank – now we go everywhere in comfortable clothes.
grammar: 'Antes la gente se vestía' – 'antes' plus the imperfect covers used-to all by itself, no extra verb needed.

target: Antes las fotos se mandaban a revelar y había que esperar una semana. Ahora la cámara guarda miles que nadie vuelve a mirar.
english: Photos used to go off to be developed and you waited a week. Now the camera stores thousands that nobody ever looks at again.
grammar: The imperfect 'se mandaban' already means used to – 'antes' sets the era, the tense does the rest.

target: Los romanos vivían en Pulborough hace siglos.
english: The Romans lived in Pulborough centuries ago.
grammar: 'Vivían' is imperfect – life carrying on over a stretch of time, dated only loosely by 'hace siglos'.

target: En otros tiempos, el panadero del barrio te fiaba si no te alcanzaba la plata.
english: In the old days, the local baker would give you credit if you didn't have enough cash.
grammar: 'En otros tiempos' plus the imperfect 'fiaba' – frame and tense both signal a repeated old habit, not one event.

target: En esa época trabajaba con dos diccionarios de papel en el escritorio y buscaba cada término a mano.
english: In those days I worked with two paper dictionaries on the desk and looked every term up by hand.
grammar: 'En esa época' calls for the imperfect: 'trabajaba' describes how things used to be, no start or end in view.

target: Cuando los chicos eran chicos, hacíamos seiscientos kilómetros con dos paradas exactas: una para comer y otra para estirar las piernas.
english: When the boys were little we'd do six hundred kilometres with exactly two stops: one for lunch and one to stretch our legs.
grammar: 'Hacíamos seiscientos kilómetros' – imperfect because this was every trip's routine, not one particular drive.

target: El padre Paul montaba obras de Navidad rarísimas con los niños.
english: Father Paul used to put on really weird Christmas plays with the children.
grammar: 'Montaba' is imperfect – the tense for what Father Paul did year after year, not one single production.

target: El lugar era lindo y el mesero muy amable, pero la cocina iba lentísima.
english: The place was lovely and the waiter very friendly, but the kitchen was dreadfully slow.
grammar: Nothing happens, everything is described – 'era lindo' and 'iba lentísima' both stay imperfect.

target: Scout creía que podía ganarle a un caballo.
english: Scout thought she could take on a horse.
grammar: Beating someone is 'ganarle a': 'podía ganarle a un caballo' – the 'le' marks the loser.

target: De joven me enfermaba cada invierno, pero ahora casi nunca me resfrío.
english: When I was young I fell ill every winter, but these days I hardly ever catch a cold.
grammar: 'Me enfermaba' – the imperfect paints the every-winter habit. A single bout would be preterite 'me enfermé'.

target: En verano siempre teníamos la casa llena: los amigos venían por un fin de semana y a veces se quedaban la semana entera.
english: In summer the house was always full – friends would come for a weekend and sometimes stay the whole week.
grammar: 'Venían' and 'se quedaban' are imperfect – summer after summer, repeated habits rather than one particular visit.

target: Tocar en una banda era divertido, aunque la familia Streeter era bastante rara.
english: Playing in a band was fun, even though the Streeter family was quite strange.
grammar: After 'aunque' a plain fact keeps the ordinary verb form: 'la familia Streeter era bastante rara' – it really was.

target: Aquella Game Boy iba con Antoine a todas partes, incluida la mesa, muy a mi pesar.
english: That Game Boy went everywhere with Antoine, including the dinner table, much to my dismay.
grammar: 'Iba con Antoine a todas partes' – the imperfect 'iba' is the went-everywhere of habit, not one trip.

target: En esa época el pan se compraba a diario y casi nadie tenía horno en la casa.
english: Back then bread was bought daily and hardly anyone had an oven at home.
grammar: 'Se compraba a diario' – the imperfect paints the old routine: back-then habits take -aba forms, not the preterite.

target: El aeropuerto era un caos: la gente corría de una puerta a otra sin saber a cuál ir.
english: The airport was utter chaos – everyone was dashing from gate to gate with no idea which one to go to.
grammar: Scene-painting runs on the imperfect: 'era un caos' and 'corría' – no single event, just the ongoing picture.

target: De adolescentes, mis hijos hablaban un idioma compuesto casi enteramente de términos de videojuegos.
english: As teenagers, my sons spoke a language made up almost entirely of video game terms.
grammar: 'Hablaban' is the imperfect – it covers how things were across whole years, not one finished event.

target: Antes íbamos de vacaciones a Latour de France.
english: We used to go to Latour de France on holiday.
grammar: The imperfect is the used-to tense: 'íbamos' – a repeated holiday habit, not one particular trip.

target: Según los vecinos, antes este barrio era mucho más tranquilo. A mí me gusta igual.
english: According to the neighbours, this area used to be much quieter – I like it all the same.
grammar: The imperfect paints old states: 'este barrio era mucho más tranquilo' – used to be, no extra verb needed.

target: Cuando mis hijos eran chicos vivíamos en el campo. Ahora cada uno anda por su lado.
english: When my children were little we lived in the countryside – now they're all off doing their own thing.
grammar: 'Eran' and 'vivíamos' are both imperfect – an era described from the inside, no start or end in sight.

target: Scout no era la perra más observadora del mundo.
english: Scout wasn't the most observant of dogs.
grammar: Past descriptions take the imperfect: 'no era' – what Scout was like, not something that happened.

target: Antes las películas las elegía Antoine, y casi nunca nos tocaba una normal.
english: Antoine always used to choose the films, and it was hardly ever a normal one.
grammar: 'Antes' cues the imperfect: 'elegía' and 'tocaba' sketch how things used to run, no end point stated.

target: De niña las clases empezaban en septiembre, así que todavía me confundo cuando acá arrancan en marzo.
english: When I was little, school started in September, so I still get confused when classes here begin in March.
grammar: 'Empezaban' is imperfect – a yearly routine back then, not one event, so the past takes the used-to form.

target: Pensaba pasar por el banco hoy, pero se me fue el día entero en llamadas.
english: I meant to drop by the bank today, but the whole day disappeared in phone calls.
grammar: 'Pensaba pasar' – the imperfect states the plan as it stood, leaving room for it never to come off.

target: Antes esta zona vivía del hierro y de la madera. Ahora vive de sus paisajes.
english: This area once lived off iron and timber. Now it lives off its landscapes.
grammar: The imperfect 'vivía' paints the old normal – 'antes' opens it, and the 'ahora' clause closes it off.

target: El Brexit siempre salía en la sobremesa, pero ya sale menos.
english: Brexit used to keep coming up at the dinner table, but it comes up less these days.
grammar: The imperfect 'salía' paints the old habit; the present 'sale' says how things are now.

target: Antes las tardes eran más claras a esta hora, ya se siente que viene el invierno.
english: The evenings used to be lighter at this time – you can tell winter's on its way.
grammar: 'Antes las tardes eran' – 'antes' + imperfect is the used-to frame, set against how things feel now ('se siente').

target: Anoche a las siete el cielo todavía estaba naranja y la calle olía a lluvia.
english: At seven last night the sky was still orange and the street smelled of rain.
grammar: 'Estaba' and 'olía' are imperfect – pure scene-painting at seven o'clock, with no event to move time along.

target: De pequeño, Antoine intentaba robarnos los helados.
english: When he was small, Antoine used to try to steal our ice creams.
grammar: 'De pequeño' packs when-he-was-little into two words; the full 'cuando era pequeño' isn't needed.

target: Antes comprábamos el queso en el mercado, ahora casi todo sale del supermercado.
english: We used to buy our cheese at the market – now nearly everything comes from the supermarket.
grammar: 'Comprábamos' – the imperfect for a past routine, what we used to do, with no endpoint in sight.

target: Scout tenía opiniones políticas bastante firmes.
english: Scout had some strong political opinions.
grammar: Ongoing past states sit in the imperfect: 'tenía' – Scout held those opinions, they didn't happen once.

target: Estaba buscando cilantro, pero solo veo perejil. ¿No le queda?
english: I was looking for coriander but I can only see parsley – have you none left?
grammar: 'Estaba buscando' – 'estaba' plus the -ando form means 'I was looking', a search still going on at that moment.

target: Al principio hacía azulejos lisos, sin dibujo, solo para agarrarle la mano al grosor.
english: At first I made plain tiles with no pattern, just to get the hang of the thickness.
grammar: 'Al principio hacía' – the imperfect covers an early stage that lasted a while, not one act of making.

target: La luz de la costa cambiaba tan rápido que los bocetos se me quedaban a medias.
english: The light on the coast would change so fast that my sketches kept ending up half-finished.
grammar: 'Cambiaba' – the imperfect covers what kept happening back then, the would-change of English habit.

target: ¿A cómo está el dólar hoy? Ayer estaba un poquito mejor.
english: What's the dollar rate today? It was a little better yesterday.
grammar: 'Ayer estaba un poquito mejor' – imperfect 'estaba' for how the rate stood, a state, not an event.

target: Cuando los chicos no querían comerse algo, les poníamos un cronómetro en la mesa.
english: When the boys didn't want to eat something, we'd put a timer on the table.
grammar: Whenever-routines go imperfect on both sides: 'no querían', 'les poníamos' – a repeated scene, not one night.

target: En las fotos la habitación se veía amplia y luminosa. En persona es otra historia.
english: In the photos the room looked spacious and bright – in the flesh it's another story.
grammar: 'Se veía amplia' – the imperfect fits how the room looked in the photos: pure description, nothing happens.

target: Antes pintaba solo en vacaciones, y ahora no dejo pasar una semana sin abrir la caja de pinturas.
english: I used to paint only on holiday, and now I don't let a week go by without opening my paintbox.
grammar: 'Pintaba' needs no used-to word – the imperfect ending alone marks the old habit that 'ahora' breaks.

target: Cuando vivíamos en Lyon, hacíamos las compras en el mercado del barrio y conocíamos a todos los puesteros.
english: When we lived in Lyon we did our shopping at the local market and knew all the stallholders.
grammar: One era, all imperfect: 'vivíamos', 'hacíamos', 'conocíamos' – background life with no single event in it.

target: Antes las llamadas de larga distancia costaban una fortuna y hablábamos cinco minutos contados. Ahora nos vemos por videollamada sin pagar nada.
english: Long-distance calls used to cost a fortune, so we'd talk for exactly five minutes. Now we see each other on video without paying a penny.
grammar: 'Costaban' and 'hablábamos' are imperfect – how things used to be, stretches of past with no start or end in view.

target: Había un saco morado con botones dorados en la vitrina, precioso.
english: There was a purple jacket with gold buttons in the shop window – gorgeous.
grammar: 'Había' is 'hay' in the imperfect – the jacket was simply there in the shop window, scenery rather than event.

target: Crié a dos hijos mientras trabajaba jornadas largas como traductora independiente.
english: I raised two sons while working long days as a freelance translator.
grammar: 'Crié' is preterite – one completed feat; 'trabajaba' is imperfect – the ongoing backdrop it happened against.

target: Nos bajamos en la parada equivocada porque el mapa del celular no cargaba.
english: We got off at the wrong stop because the map on my phone wouldn't load.
grammar: 'Nos bajamos' is the event, 'no cargaba' the ongoing glitch behind it – two pasts, two jobs.

target: Salía del supermercado cuando me alcanzó la cajera: se me había quedado una bolsa en la caja.
english: I was just leaving the supermarket when the cashier caught up with me: I'd left one of my bags at the till.
grammar: 'Salía' on its own already means I was just leaving – no need for 'estaba', the tense does it alone.

target: Cuando compramos la casa de Josselin, nadie se imaginaba el trabajo que le íbamos a meter.
english: When we bought the Josselin house, nobody imagined the work we were going to put into it.
grammar: 'Compramos' lands the one-off purchase, 'nadie se imaginaba' the mindset around it – event versus backdrop.

target: Íbamos por la mitad de la caminata cuando empezó a caer un aguacero, así que nos refugiamos bajo un árbol hasta que pasó.
english: We were halfway through the walk when a downpour started, so we sheltered under a tree until it passed.
grammar: 'Íbamos por la mitad' – the imperfect parks the walk halfway, and 'empezó' drops the event into the middle of it.

target: Este azulejo se agrietó porque el horno estaba demasiado caliente.
english: This tile cracked because the kiln was too hot.
grammar: 'Se agrietó' is the sudden event, 'estaba' the standing condition – one crack against ongoing heat.

target: Cuando llegamos no había ninguna mesa libre, así que esperamos en la barra.
english: When we arrived there wasn't a single free table, so we waited at the bar.
grammar: 'Llegamos' and 'esperamos' are the events – 'no había ninguna mesa' paints the scene they ran into.

target: Llevaba tantos cables en la mochila que en seguridad me hicieron vaciarla enterita.
english: I had so many cables in my rucksack that at security they made me empty the whole thing out.
grammar: 'Llevaba' (imperfect) sets the standing state, and 'me hicieron' (preterite) is the one event that lands in it.

target: Antoine hizo como que se iba a comer una caca de oveja, y de verdad le creí.
english: Antoine pretended he was going to eat sheep poo, and I actually believed he was about to do it.
grammar: 'Se iba a comer' – imperfect 'iba' means was-about-to; the eating never lands, which is the whole joke.

target: Salí sin chaqueta porque hacía sol, y claro, a media tarde cayó un aguacero.
english: I went out without a jacket because it was sunny – and of course, mid-afternoon there was a downpour.
grammar: 'Hacía sol' sets the weather backdrop while 'salí' and 'cayó' move the story – scene-setting takes the imperfect.

target: Subíamos una cuesta en Georgia cuando el motor del carro empezó a echar humo.
english: We were going up a hill in Georgia when the car engine started smoking.
grammar: 'Subíamos' sets the moving backdrop, 'empezó' fires the event inside it – scene in imperfect, action in preterite.

target: Cuando traducía contratos, aprendí a leer la letra chica.
english: When I translated contracts, I learned to read the fine print.
grammar: 'Traducía' is the long backdrop, 'aprendí' the single event that happened against it.

target: Mientras el cielo se oscurecía, alcancé a apuntar los colores en una esquina del boceto.
english: While the sky was darkening, I just managed to jot the colours down in a corner of the sketch.
grammar: 'Se oscurecía' sets the ongoing backdrop and 'alcancé' is the one event inside it – imperfect frames, preterite acts.

target: Al principio pensaba igual que tú, pero cuando lo vi con mis propios ojos cambié de opinión.
english: At first I thought the same as you, but once I saw it with my own eyes I changed my mind.
grammar: 'Pensaba' is the ongoing belief, 'cambié' the one-off act that ended it – the two past tenses in one line.

target: Estaba ordenando el taller cuando de repente se fue la luz, y mejor lo dejé para la mañana.
english: I was tidying the workshop when all of a sudden the power went off, so I just left it till the morning.
grammar: 'Estaba ordenando' stretches across the scene until 'se fue la luz' lands – ongoing imperfect, sudden preterite.

target: Ya iba llegando al banco cuando me di cuenta de que había dejado la billetera en la casa, así que me devolví por ella.
english: I was nearly at the bank when I realised I'd left my purse at home, so I went back for it.
grammar: 'iba llegando' stretches the almost-there moment, then 'me di cuenta' cuts in – imperfect meets preterite.

target: Ayer compré unos mangos que estaban perfectos. ¿Le quedan de esos?
english: I bought some mangoes yesterday that were just perfect – do you have any of those left?
grammar: 'Compré' is the one-off purchase, 'estaban' how the mangoes were – deed in preterite, state in imperfect.

target: Me estaba bañando cuando se cortó el agua. Así cualquiera pierde la paciencia.
english: I was in the middle of a shower when the water went off – enough to try anyone's patience.
grammar: 'Me estaba bañando' is the action mid-flow and 'se cortó' the cut-in – past progressive meets preterite.

target: Estaba mostrándoles el jardín a los invitados cuando empezó a llover, así que seguimos la visita adentro con un té.
english: I was showing our guests round the garden when it started to rain, so we carried on the tour indoors over a cup of tea.
grammar: 'Estaba mostrándoles' is the backdrop in progress – 'empezó a llover' cuts in as a one-off, so it goes preterite.

target: Antes llamábamos a un técnico para todo, hasta que quedó claro que Ken lo hacía mejor.
english: We used to call someone in for everything, until it became clear Ken did it better.
grammar: 'llamábamos' paints the long-running habit, 'quedó claro' the moment it ended – imperfect versus preterite at work.

target: Íbamos perdiendo la tradición familiar, hasta que el tenis de mesa nos salvó.
english: We were losing the family tradition, until table tennis saved us.
grammar: 'Íbamos perdiendo' drifts along in the imperfect – the preterite 'nos salvó' is the event that ends it.

target: Por fin apareció la maleta. Ya me estaba imaginando toda la semana con la misma ropa.
english: The suitcase finally turned up – I was already picturing the whole week in the same clothes.
grammar: 'Apareció' is the one-off event, 'estaba imaginando' the scene already running in the background.

target: Un carro giró sin avisar justo cuando yo iba a cruzar, menos mal que alcancé a verlo.
english: A car turned without indicating just as I was about to cross – luckily I spotted it in time.
grammar: 'Iba a cruzar' – imperfect 'ir a' means was about to: the crossing was still pending when the car 'giró'.

target: De vuelta a casa manejaba con calma cuando un ciclista se me cruzó de repente, y menos mal que alcancé a frenar.
english: On the way home I was driving along calmly when a cyclist cut right in front of me, and thank goodness I managed to brake in time.
grammar: 'Alcancé a frenar' – 'alcanzar a' + infinitive is managing something just in time, the preterite catching the moment.

target: Cuando recién empecé, contaba las brazadas para no pensar en el frío.
english: When I first started I used to count my strokes to keep my mind off the cold.
grammar: 'Empecé' is the single starting point, 'contaba' the routine that filled the weeks after – event, then habit.

target: Fui a un paseo en velero precioso, y esta vez no estaba esa señora tan pesada.
english: I went on a lovely sailing trip, and this time that terribly annoying woman wasn't there.
grammar: 'Fui' moves the story (one trip); 'no estaba' sets the scene – the preterite–imperfect division of labour.

target: Desde lejos la plaza se veía cerquita, pero caminando tardamos casi veinte minutos.
english: From a distance the square looked really close, but on foot it took us nearly twenty minutes.
grammar: 'Se veía cerquita' – impressions run in the imperfect, while 'tardamos' logs the fact that proved it wrong.

target: Cuando llegamos a la costa, el cielo estaba despejado, pero de repente se nubló.
english: When we got to the coast the sky was clear, but it suddenly clouded over.
grammar: 'Estaba despejado' paints the standing scene – 'llegamos' and 'se nubló' are the events that cut through it.

target: Se fue la luz justo cuando el aceite estaba en su punto, así que tocó apagar todo.
english: The power went off just when the oil was at the right temperature, so it all had to be switched off.
grammar: 'Se fue la luz' is the sudden event, 'estaba en su punto' the ongoing backdrop – preterite cuts across the imperfect.

target: Cuando llegamos a lo alto de la colina, el sol apenas estaba saliendo, así que paramos un momento a mirar.
english: When we reached the top of the hill the sun was only just coming up, so we stopped for a moment to take it in.
grammar: 'Llegamos' and 'paramos' move the story along, 'estaba saliendo' is the slow backdrop behind them.

target: El pantalón me quedaba perfecto hasta que lo lavé con agua caliente, ahora me aprieta por todos lados.
english: The trousers fitted perfectly until I washed them in hot water – now they're tight everywhere.
grammar: 'Me quedaba perfecto' ran on until one event ended it: 'hasta que' + preterite 'lavé' cuts a state short.

target: Apenas prendimos las velas, ya media sala estaba grabando con el celular.
english: The moment we lit the candles, half the room was already filming on their phones.
grammar: 'Prendimos' is the one-off preterite event, while 'estaba grabando' paints the action already under way.

target: Oiga, ¿qué anunciaron por el parlante? Hablaban tan rápido que no capté ni la mitad.
english: Sorry, what did they announce over the loudspeaker? They were speaking so fast I caught barely half of it.
grammar: 'Anunciaron' names the one-off event, 'hablaban' the ongoing manner – preterite and imperfect share one scene.

target: Antoine esperaba en la puerta cuando llegó el paquete con la Game Boy, y el grito se oyó en todo el barrio.
english: Antoine was waiting by the door when the Game Boy parcel arrived, and the shout could be heard across the whole neighbourhood.
grammar: 'Esperaba' holds the scene open until 'llegó' happens inside it – backdrop imperfect, event preterite.

target: No sabía cuánto se dejaba de propina aquí, así que pregunté en el hotel.
english: I didn't know how much people tip here, so I asked at the hotel.
grammar: 'No sabía' stretches across time, 'pregunté' is the single act that ended it – imperfect vs preterite.

target: Busqué los guantes por toda la casa y al final estaban en el bolsillo del abrigo.
english: I hunted for the gloves all over the house and in the end they were in the coat pocket.
grammar: 'Busqué' wraps up the finished hunt, 'estaban' tells where the gloves sat all along – past location leans imperfect.

target: Ken acababa de alisar el césped cuando apareció un montículo nuevo justo en el medio.
english: Ken had just levelled the lawn when a fresh molehill appeared right in the middle.
grammar: 'acababa de alisar' – imperfect 'acabar de' means had just done, and the preterite 'apareció' interrupts it.

target: Iba a hacer una ensalada, pero la lechuga ya estaba marchita, así que compré otra.
english: I was going to make a salad, but the lettuce had already gone limp, so I bought another one.
grammar: 'Iba a hacer' – the imperfect holds a plan that never happened, then preterite 'compré' logs what did.

target: Volvía cansada del centro, pero había música en vivo en la plaza y se me alegró el día.
english: I was coming back from town feeling tired, but there was live music in the square and it brightened my whole day.
grammar: 'Volvía' and 'había' set the scene mid-flow – 'se me alegró' is the preterite event that broke into it.

target: Estaba ordenando el ropero cuando encontré una bufanda que daba por perdida desde el invierno pasado.
english: I was tidying the wardrobe when I found a scarf I'd given up for lost last winter.
grammar: 'Estaba ordenando' – 'estaba' plus the -ando form paints you mid-task, the job 'encontré' walks in on.

target: El vuelo estaba programado para las diez, pero lo cambiaron a las ocho sin avisar.
english: The flight was scheduled for ten, but they switched it to eight without warning.
grammar: 'Estaba programado' sets the scene and 'lo cambiaron' is the one-off event – imperfect and preterite in one sentence.

target: Cuando era niña me operaron de apendicitis, por si le sirve para la historia clínica.
english: I had my appendix out as a child, in case that's useful for my medical notes.
grammar: 'Era niña' is the backdrop age and 'me operaron' the one-off event inside it – imperfect frame, preterite deed.

target: Pensábamos que el feriado caía viernes, pero al revisar el calendario resultó que era jueves.
english: We thought the holiday fell on the Friday, but when we checked the calendar it turned out to be the Thursday.
grammar: 'Caía' (imperfect) is what we kept assuming – 'resultó' (preterite) is the moment it turned out otherwise.

target: La receta decía cuarenta minutos de horno, pero saqué el pastel a los treinta y quedó en su punto.
english: The recipe said forty minutes in the oven, but I took the cake out at thirty and it was spot on.
grammar: 'Decía' is imperfect for what the recipe stated all along – 'saqué' is the one-off decision that cut it short.

target: Cuando salimos de Portsmouth llovía a cántaros, y al llegar a Bretaña nos recibió un sol espléndido.
english: When we left Portsmouth it was pouring down, and when we got to Brittany we were met by glorious sunshine.
grammar: 'Salimos' is one clean event, 'llovía' the weather running behind it – downpours are classic imperfect scenery.

target: Estábamos en plena conversación cuando se cortó la llamada, entonces le mandé un mensaje para terminar de contarle.
english: We were mid-conversation when the call dropped, so I sent her a message to finish telling her.
grammar: 'Estábamos en plena conversación' means we were mid-conversation – 'en plena' puts you right in the middle.

target: El mar estaba movido durante el cruce, así que casi nadie desayunó a bordo.
english: The sea was rough during the crossing, so hardly anyone had breakfast on board.
grammar: 'Estaba movido' paints the scene, 'desayunó' logs the outcome – states take imperfect, events take the preterite.

target: Mientras la primera tanda se enfriaba, preparé los esmaltes para la segunda.
english: While the first batch was cooling, I got the glazes ready for the second.
grammar: 'Se enfriaba' keeps running while 'preparé' happens whole – two past tenses splitting the two jobs.

target: El agua estaba tan fría esta mañana que solo aguantamos diez minutos.
english: The water was so cold this morning that we only managed ten minutes.
grammar: 'Estaba' paints the water's state, 'aguantamos' closes the ten minutes – open description, finished stretch.

target: Anoche, cuando ya estábamos cenando, tocaron la puerta dos peregrinos jóvenes de lo más raros.
english: Last night, when we were already having dinner, two very odd young pilgrims knocked at the door.
grammar: 'Ya estábamos cenando' paints the scene in progress, then 'tocaron la puerta' cuts in – imperfect meets preterite.

target: Estaba peleándome con el mapa cuando un señor se acercó a ayudarme. ¡Qué amable es la gente acá!
english: I was wrestling with the map when a gentleman came over to help me – people here are so kind!
grammar: 'Estaba peleándome' sets the scene mid-action and 'se acercó' cuts in – imperfect backdrop, preterite event.

target: El puesto de quesos siempre estaba en la misma esquina, pero esta semana lo cambiaron de lugar y me costó encontrarlo.
english: The cheese stall was always on the same corner, but this week they moved it and it took me a while to find.
grammar: 'Siempre estaba' – imperfect for the standing arrangement, then 'cambiaron' records the one week that broke it.

target: Justo cuando salíamos del agua, apareció el sol y el mar entero cambió de color.
english: Just as we were getting out of the water the sun came out and the whole sea changed colour.
grammar: 'Justo cuando salíamos' catches the action midway – imperfect – and 'apareció' is what struck at that instant.

target: ¡Qué suerte que estaba en Londres investigando para la audioguía justo cuando Antoine se enfermó! Le conseguí el remedio ese mismo día.
english: What luck that I was in London researching the audioguide just when Antoine fell ill: I got him his medicine that very day.
grammar: 'Se enfermó' is the sudden event and 'estaba en Londres investigando' the scene it lands in – the classic past pairing.

target: Iba tan concentrada en las riendas que ni me di cuenta de que había empezado a llover.
english: I was so busy concentrating on the reins that I didn't even notice it had started raining.
grammar: 'Iba tan concentrada' is imperfect backdrop, and preterite 'me di cuenta' is the event that lands against it.

target: Mientras traducía el discurso, me di cuenta de que una cifra del original estaba mal.
english: While I was translating the speech, I noticed one of the figures in the original was wrong.
grammar: 'Mientras traducía' rolls along in the background while 'me di cuenta' lands once – the imperfect–preterite split.

target: Justo cuando salíamos de la casa, sonó el teléfono, así que llegamos tarde al almuerzo.
english: Just as we were leaving the house the phone rang, so we were late for lunch.
grammar: 'Salíamos' holds the leaving open mid-action and 'sonó' cuts in – interruptions pair imperfect with preterite.

target: Cuando llegué al acantilado, la luz era justo la que buscaba, así que me quedé pintando hasta el atardecer.
english: When I got to the cliff the light was just what I was after, so I stayed painting until sunset.
grammar: 'Llegué' moves the story forward, then 'era' simply describes the light found there – no start, no finish.

target: Cuando empecé con la equitación, la clase costaba veinticinco libras, y hoy no baja de cuarenta.
english: When I took up riding, a lesson cost twenty-five pounds, and these days you won't get one for under forty.
grammar: 'Empecé' pins the one-off starting point – 'costaba' is imperfect for the price that was simply true back then.

target: Estaba guardando el celular cuando entró la videollamada de mi hijo, así que me senté en una banca a contestarle.
english: I was just putting my phone away when a video call from my son came in, so I sat down on a bench to answer it.
grammar: 'Estaba guardando' paints the scene mid-action – the call that cut in, 'entró', takes the one-off preterite.

target: Había tanto ruido en la avenida que nos alejamos unas cuadras y encontramos una placita tranquila.
english: There was so much noise on the avenue that we moved a few blocks away and found a quiet little square.
grammar: Scene-setters go imperfect: 'había tanto ruido' – then the response, 'nos alejamos', lands in the preterite.

target: Me probé la falda en la tienda y me quedaba muy bien, pero ya en la casa no me convenció.
english: I tried the skirt on in the shop and it fitted really well, but back at home I just wasn't convinced.
grammar: 'Me probé' is a one-off act, 'me quedaba muy bien' the ongoing state – how clothes fitted stays in the imperfect.

target: Benoît iba perdiendo, y de repente aparecieron dos cartas en su manga.
english: Benoît was losing, and suddenly two cards appeared from his sleeve.
grammar: 'Iba perdiendo' paints the ongoing backdrop, then preterite 'aparecieron' lands the event that moves the story.

target: Yo era gran maestra de judo y entrené con los grandes sabios Masako y John Harrison.
english: I used to be a judo grandmaster – I trained with the great sages Masako and John Harrison.
grammar: 'Era' paints the ongoing state, 'entrené' logs the one-off feat – imperfect and preterite share the sentence.

target: El semáforo cambió cuando íbamos por la mitad de la calle, así que nos tocó apurarnos.
english: The lights changed when we were halfway across the street, so we had to get a move on.
grammar: 'Cambió' is the one sharp event, 'íbamos' the crossing already in motion – interruptions take the preterite.

target: Como la acera estaba levantada por las obras, ese tramo lo hicimos por la calle.
english: As the pavement was dug up for the roadworks, we did that stretch in the road.
grammar: 'Estaba levantada' is a standing state, so imperfect – the one-off answer, 'lo hicimos', takes the preterite.

target: Justo cuando el electricista estaba revisando el medidor, la luz volvió sola.
english: Just as the electrician was checking the meter, the power came back on by itself.
grammar: 'Estaba revisando' stretches on in the background – the preterite 'volvió' is the event that breaks in on it.

target: Estaba imprimiendo los boletos tan tranquila cuando la impresora se quedó sin papel.
english: There I was, happily printing the tickets, when the printer ran out of paper.
grammar: 'Estaba imprimiendo' has the scene mid-action when 'se quedó' cuts in – interruptions take the preterite.

target: Nunca supimos de dónde sacaba Pierre los nombres de sus peluches, pero Courtpartout se quedó para siempre.
english: We never did find out where Pierre got his soft toys' names from, but Courtpartout stuck forever.
grammar: 'Nunca supimos' seals the outcome while 'sacaba' keeps the old habit running – both pasts in one sentence.

target: Estaba puliendo el último párrafo cuando me avisaron que el plazo se había adelantado un día.
english: I was polishing the final paragraph when they let me know the deadline had been brought forward a day.
grammar: 'Estaba puliendo' stretches the scene out, then 'me avisaron' cuts in – ongoing imperfect, interrupting preterite.

target: ¿Ha visto lo que cuestan unas botas de cuero hoy en día? Mejor mando a arreglar estas.
english: Have you seen what leather boots cost these days? I'd rather have these repaired.
grammar: 'Ha visto' – 'haber' + participle ties past experience to the present moment: prices as they stand these days.

target: Es la primera vez que vengo a Sudamérica y me ha sorprendido lo verde que es todo.
english: It's my first time in South America, and I've been struck by how green everything is.
grammar: 'Me ha sorprendido' – a still-open trip keeps its surprises in the perfect, where 'sorprendió' would close them off.

target: Hemos cruzado el canal tantas veces que los del ferry ya nos saludan.
english: We've crossed the Channel so many times that the ferry crew greet us now.
grammar: 'Hemos cruzado' – the perfect counts crossings up to now, an open total that is still growing.

target: Han anunciado por los parlantes que nuestro vuelo está demorado, pero todavía no dicen cuánto.
english: They've announced over the loudspeakers that our flight is delayed, but they still haven't said by how much.
grammar: 'Han anunciado' – the perfect suits news that just landed and still matters: the delay is running right now.

target: Nunca hemos cancelado por frío: por niebla sí, un par de veces, porque no se veía nada.
english: We've never called it off because of the cold: fog, yes, a couple of times, because you couldn't see a thing.
grammar: 'Nunca hemos cancelado' – the perfect with 'nunca' sweeps the whole record up to today: not once, so far.

target: ¿Te has dado cuenta de lo rápido que se ha ido el año? Parece que enero fue la semana pasada.
english: Have you noticed how quickly the year has gone? It feels like January was last week.
grammar: 'Se ha ido' – 'haber' plus participle ties the past to now: the year has gone and you feel it in the present.

target: En el comedero de Marescot hemos visto de todo: herrerillos, carboneros, jilgueros y hasta un arrendajo.
english: At the Marescot feeder we have seen all sorts: blue tits, great tits, goldfinches and even a jay.
grammar: 'hemos visto de todo' – the perfect keeps a running list open: sightings so far, with more birds free to join.

target: ¿Cómo se dice esto en español? La he escuchado mil veces y nunca me acuerdo.
english: How do you say this in Spanish? I've heard the word a thousand times and I can never remember it.
grammar: 'La he escuchado mil veces' – the perfect gathers repeats that reach into now, not one closed-off occasion.

target: Twig no ha leído la constitución, pero la defiende con una convicción admirable.
english: Twig hasn't read the constitution, but he defends it with admirable conviction.
grammar: 'No ha leído' – the perfect measures up to now: no reading yet, still possible. 'No leyó' would close the case.

target: Últimamente he comprado mucho plátano maduro para freír, como lo preparan aquí.
english: Lately I've been buying lots of ripe plantain for frying, the way they make it here.
grammar: 'He comprado' pairs with 'últimamente' – the perfect covers a recent stretch that reaches up to now.

target: Ya han llegado los primeros invitados y todavía no terminamos de poner la mesa.
english: The first guests have already arrived and we still haven't finished laying the table.
grammar: 'Ya han llegado' – 'ya' with the perfect announces fresh already-done news that still matters now.

target: He encargado el pastel para las cinco, así que hay que pasar a recogerlo sin falta.
english: I've ordered the cake for five o'clock, so we really must go and collect it.
grammar: 'He encargado' – perfect, not preterite, because the ordering still touches now: the cake awaits pickup.

target: Esta semana he llamado tres veces al banco y todavía no me han confirmado la cita del lunes catorce.
english: I've rung the bank three times this week and they still haven't confirmed my appointment for Monday the fourteenth.
grammar: 'Todavía no me han confirmado' – 'todavía no' with the perfect flags a still-pending event: it could yet happen.

target: He ido construyendo mi negocio de traducción poco a poco.
english: I've built up my translation business bit by bit.
grammar: 'He ido construyendo' – 'ir' plus the -ndo form paints gradual progress: building it up bit by bit.

target: Todavía no he terminado el cuadro del puerto.
english: I still haven't finished the painting of the harbour.
grammar: 'Todavía no he terminado' – not-yet pairs with the perfect: unfinished business stays linked to now.

target: Pedimos hace veinte minutos y todavía no nos han traído ni el pan.
english: We ordered twenty minutes ago and they haven't even brought us the bread yet.
grammar: 'No nos han traído' – the perfect keeps the complaint live: the bread is still missing right now.

target: ¿Han pensado dónde celebrar el aniversario, o siguen comparando restaurantes?
english: Have you thought about where to celebrate the anniversary, or are you still comparing restaurants?
grammar: 'Han pensado' – the perfect suits a have-you-yet question, the deciding may or may not have happened.

target: ¿Alguna vez has tomado uno de esos mototaxis? No sé si atreverme.
english: Have you ever taken one of those mototaxis? I'm not sure I'd dare.
grammar: 'Alguna vez has tomado' – 'alguna vez' plus the perfect is the set frame for have you ever.

target: Nunca me he vacunado contra la fiebre amarilla. ¿La exigen para entrar a la selva?
english: I've never had a yellow fever jab – do they require it for going into the jungle?
grammar: 'Nunca me he vacunado' – 'nunca' with the perfect spans a whole life up to now: never yet, still possible.

target: No he pasado todavía por el puente nuevo, dicen que la vista al atardecer vale la pena.
english: I still haven't been over the new bridge – they say the view at sunset is worth it.
grammar: 'No he pasado todavía' – the perfect for still-open business: the bridge visit is pending, not history.

target: Antoine ha perdido otro objeto de valor. De verdad es un caso perdido.
english: Antoine has lost yet another valuable item – he really is a lost cause.
grammar: 'Ha perdido otro' – a running tally reaching into the present, so even Latin American Spanish picks the perfect.

target: El agua ha estado más templada esta semana, se nota que por fin llegó el verano de verdad.
english: The water's been warmer this week, you can tell summer has properly arrived at last.
grammar: 'Esta semana' reaches into today, so the perfect fits: 'ha estado' – a warm spell not yet closed off.

target: Antoine ha vuelto a dejar el formulario 'para el fin de semana'. Van doce fines de semana.
english: Antoine has once again left the form 'for the weekend'. That's twelve weekends now.
grammar: Doing something again is 'volver a': 'ha vuelto a dejar' – has left it yet again, repeat built into volver.

target: Nunca he logrado que un cielo gris se vea interesante, pero sigo intentándolo.
english: I've never managed to make a grey sky look interesting, but I keep trying.
grammar: 'Nunca he logrado' – 'nunca' plus the perfect covers your whole life up to now: never managed it yet.

target: Está bien, lo admito: nunca he probado ese plato, así que mejor me guardo mi opinión.
english: Fair enough, I admit it – I've never tried that dish, so I'd best keep my opinion to myself.
grammar: 'Nunca he probado' – the perfect sums up life so far: not once, up to and including now.

target: Esta semana he estado arreglando el cuarto de los invitados: solo falta ponerle unas flores a la mesita de noche.
english: This week I've been getting the guest room ready – all that's left is to put some flowers on the bedside table.
grammar: 'He estado arreglando' – the perfect fits a still-open stretch like 'esta semana': the tidying reaches into now.

target: Todavía no me han pagado la factura de marzo, y ya va siendo hora de mandar un recordatorio.
english: They still haven't paid my March invoice, and it's about time I sent a reminder.
grammar: 'Todavía no me han pagado' – the perfect keeps the situation open into now, exactly what 'todavía no' needs.

target: ¿Has asado verduras a la parrilla alguna vez? Quedan dulces y con un toque ahumado.
english: Have you ever roasted vegetables on the grill? They come out sweet, with a smoky edge.
grammar: 'Alguna vez' pairs with the perfect 'has asado' – the ever-question, where any time up to now counts.

target: Hemos organizado la fiesta entre varios, así que nadie ha tenido que gastar de más.
english: We've organised the party between several of us, so nobody has had to overspend.
grammar: 'Hemos organizado' – haber does the agreeing (hemos = we), while 'organizado' never changes its ending.

target: Este año he salido a pasear a caballo más veces que en los tres años anteriores juntos.
english: This year I've been out riding more times than in the previous three years put together.
grammar: 'Este año' is still open, so the perfect counts inside it: 'he salido' – rides tallied up to now.

target: Nunca he visto el mar tan quieto como esta mañana.
english: I've never seen the sea as still as it was this morning.
grammar: 'Nunca he visto' – a never spanning your whole life up to now calls for the perfect.

target: Todavía no he envuelto el regalo, ¿tienes por ahí cinta adhesiva?
english: I still haven't wrapped the present – have you got any sticky tape handy?
grammar: 'Envuelto' is envolver's irregular participle – like 'vuelto' from volver, no 'envolvido' exists.

target: Hasta ahora nunca he necesitado un abogado, pero dicen que conviene tener uno de confianza.
english: So far I've never needed a lawyer, but they say it's worth having one you trust.
grammar: 'Nunca he necesitado' – the perfect sweeps your whole life up to now, which is why 'hasta ahora' sits with it.

target: Ken ya ha pedido dos postres y está estudiando la carta 'por si acaso'.
english: Ken has already ordered two puddings and is studying the menu 'just in case'.
grammar: 'Ya ha pedido' – 'ya' with the present perfect means already: the deed is done inside a scene still going.

target: Mi hijo todavía no ha contestado el mensaje que le mandé esta mañana, pero seguro anda ocupado.
english: My son still hasn't answered the message I sent him this morning, but he's probably just busy.
grammar: 'Todavía no ha contestado' – present perfect keeps the not-yet open: the reply may still land.

target: Ken ha arreglado media casa con sus propias manos, y todavía le queda la otra mitad.
english: Ken has fixed half the house with his own hands, and there's still the other half to do.
grammar: 'ha arreglado' – the perfect counts work done up to now, and 'todavía le queda' keeps the job officially open.

target: Antoine nos ha puesto otra película soviética rarísima, y todavía estamos tratando de entender el final.
english: Antoine has put on yet another very strange Soviet film, and we're still trying to work out the ending.
grammar: 'nos ha puesto' – the perfect because the fallout is still live: 'todavía estamos tratando' ties it to right now.

target: He aprendido a preguntar antes que adivinar: el cliente siempre prefiere una consulta a un error.
english: I've learned to ask rather than guess: a client would always rather answer a question than find a mistake.
grammar: 'He aprendido' – the perfect ties a past lesson to the present: learned back then, still true today.

target: Nunca he llevado la cuenta de cuántos azulejos he pintado, pero seguro pasan del millar.
english: I've never kept count of how many tiles I've painted, but it's well past a thousand by now.
grammar: 'Nunca he llevado la cuenta' – 'nunca' with the present perfect covers a whole lifetime up to now, and it still holds.

target: Antoine todavía no ha instalado su bidé.
english: Antoine still hasn't installed his bidet.
grammar: For still hasn't, pair 'todavía no' with the perfect: 'todavía no ha instalado su bidé'.

target: He vuelto a empezar la boca del retrato tres veces, y todavía no me convence.
english: I've started the mouth on this portrait from scratch three times, and I'm still not happy with it.
grammar: 'He vuelto a empezar' – present perfect because the tally is live: three restarts so far, maybe more coming.

target: Nunca he cocinado con este ají, ¿pica mucho?
english: I've never cooked with this chilli – is it very hot?
grammar: 'Nunca he cocinado' – the perfect sweeps up your whole life so far: never yet, to this day.

target: Nunca hemos perdido un ferry, aunque un par de veces llegamos con los minutos contados.
english: We've never missed a ferry, though a couple of times we cut it very fine.
grammar: 'Nunca hemos perdido' keeps the record open to today – preterite 'llegamos' pins the close calls to their dates.

target: Montar no es algo que se aprenda de un día para otro: yo he ido mejorando poco a poco, clase a clase.
english: Riding isn't something you learn overnight: I've been improving bit by bit, lesson by lesson.
grammar: 'he ido mejorando' – 'ir' plus the -ando form means improving gradually: getting better lesson by lesson.

target: Todavía no he encontrado un esmalte verde que me convenza.
english: I still haven't found a green glaze I'm happy with.
grammar: 'No he encontrado' – the perfect suits a still-open search: it began in the past and is running now.

target: ¿Me está diciendo que no pasó la tarjeta? La he usado toda la mañana sin problema.
english: Are you telling me the card didn't go through? I've used it all morning without a problem.
grammar: 'La he usado toda la mañana' takes the perfect because the morning isn't finished yet.

target: Este año los topos han levantado montículos por todo el césped.
english: This year the moles have thrown up molehills all over the lawn.
grammar: 'Este año' hasn't finished yet, so the perfect fits: 'han levantado' counts damage inside an open period.

target: Ya he limpiado el piso dos veces hoy y sigue lleno de polvo por la obra de al lado.
english: I've already cleaned the floor twice today and it's still covered in dust from the building work next door.
grammar: The perfect fits a day still in progress: 'ya he limpiado el piso dos veces hoy' – today isn't over yet.

target: Pedimos toallas extra hace una hora y todavía no las han subido.
english: We asked for extra towels an hour ago and they still haven't brought them up.
grammar: 'Todavía no las han subido' – the perfect keeps the wait open: the not-arriving runs right up to now.

target: Hemos viajado bastante, pero pocas cosas se comparan con Kioto al atardecer.
english: We've travelled a fair bit, but few things compare with Kyoto at dusk.
grammar: 'Hemos viajado' – experience with no date attached: the perfect totals up life so far instead of naming one trip.

target: Este año no hemos tenido tiempo de celebrar nada, por eso queremos hacer algo especial en diciembre.
english: This year we haven't had time to celebrate anything, which is why we want to do something special in December.
grammar: With 'este año' still running, the perfect fits – 'no hemos tenido tiempo' sits inside an open period.

target: Entre Ken y yo hemos arreglado Marescot casi entero: le hemos metido horas a cada cuarto.
english: Between us, Ken and I have done up nearly all of Marescot: we have put hours into every room.
grammar: 'Hemos arreglado' – the perfect ties past work to now: what's been done to the house still stands today.

target: Esta semana he estado de buen humor, y eso que el clima no ha ayudado en nada.
english: I've been in a good mood this week, even though the weather hasn't helped one bit.
grammar: 'He estado de buen humor' – the perfect covers a stretch still open: 'esta semana' has not ended yet.

target: Muchas familias han cultivado estas tierras durante generaciones.
english: Many families have farmed this land for generations.
grammar: 'Han cultivado' pairs with 'durante generaciones' – the perfect keeps the span open right up to today.

target: He intentado conectarme tres veces y la página se queda cargando. ¿Les está fallando el internet?
english: I've tried to connect three times and the page just sits there loading – is your internet playing up?
grammar: 'He intentado conectarme tres veces' – attempts in a still-open struggle take the perfect, not a closed 'intenté'.

target: Otra vez ha amanecido una mancha amarilla en el césped: las hembras de zorro han pasado de visita.
english: Another yellow patch on the lawn this morning: the vixens have been visiting.
grammar: 'han pasado de visita' – the perfect flags fresh evidence: the visit is over but its trace is on today's lawn.

target: Ya me he acostumbrado a cambiar de lado al manejar: por la izquierda en Inglaterra y por la derecha en Francia.
english: I've got used to switching sides when I drive: on the left in England and on the right in France.
grammar: 'Ya me he acostumbrado' – 'ya' with the present perfect marks a change complete and still in force right now.

target: Hoy no he revisado el correo todavía. De seguro hay como veinte mensajes esperando.
english: I haven't checked my email yet today. There are bound to be a good twenty messages waiting.
grammar: 'No he revisado el correo todavía' – the perfect for a day still in progress: the checking can still happen.

target: Ken ha sido muy constante con el ciclismo y las salidas a correr.
english: Ken has been very good about cycling and running consistently.
grammar: 'ha sido' – has been and still is: the present perfect keeps Ken's streak running right up to now.

target: Los videojuegos les han arruinado la vida a mis hijos para siempre. De vez en cuando los saludo por el pasillo.
english: Video games have ruined my sons' lives forever – now and then I greet them in the hallway.
grammar: 'Les han arruinado la vida' – the perfect ties a past act to the present: the damage is still in force.

target: El aire acondicionado no ha funcionado desde que llegamos. ¿Podrían mandar a alguien a revisarlo?
english: The air conditioning hasn't worked since we arrived – could you send someone to look at it?
grammar: 'No ha funcionado desde que' – the present perfect pairs with 'desde' to run the fault from arrival to now.

target: Bajé las escaleras del malecón a toda prisa, pero la lancha del paseo ya había zarpado.
english: I dashed down the steps to the waterfront, but the tour boat had already set off.
grammar: 'Ya había zarpado' – 'ya' sits just before the pair: 'había' and its participle travel together, unsplit.

target: Cuando por fin logré conectarme, los demás ya habían empezado sin mí y no me enteré de la mitad.
english: By the time I finally got connected, the others had already started without me and I missed half of it.
grammar: 'Ya habían empezado' – past perfect for the earlier of two pasts: their start came before 'logré conectarme'.

target: Para cuando encontré el tono exacto del mar, ya había gastado medio tubo de azul.
english: By the time I found the exact shade of the sea, I'd already gone through half a tube of blue.
grammar: 'Ya había gastado' – the pluperfect marks what was already done before 'encontré', the earlier of two pasts.

target: ¡Qué alivio! Creí que había perdido el pasaporte, pero estaba en el fondo del bolso.
english: What a relief – I thought I'd lost my passport, but it was at the bottom of my bag.
grammar: 'Creí que había perdido' – 'había' + participle sets the loss before the moment of believing it.

target: Cuando volvimos del paseo, Beni ya se había comido su cena.
english: By the time we got back from the walk, Beni had already eaten her dinner.
grammar: 'Ya se había comido' – 'había' + participle steps one layer further back: eaten before we even returned.

target: Cuando por fin llegamos a la casa, el pasto ya había crecido hasta las rodillas.
english: By the time we finally got to the house, the grass had grown up to our knees.
grammar: 'Ya había crecido' – 'había' + participle sets the growing before the arriving, two layers of past in one line.

target: Cuando llamé para pedir ayuda, la pantalla ya se había arreglado sola. Qué vergüenza.
english: By the time I rang for help, the screen had already sorted itself out. How embarrassing.
grammar: 'Ya se había arreglado' – the pluperfect for the fix that beat the call: one step further back than 'llamé'.

target: Cuando abrí el horno, el esmalte ya se había corrido hacia los bordes.
english: When I opened the kiln, the glaze had already run to the edges.
grammar: 'Ya se había corrido' – 'ya' plus the pluperfect means the damage predated the moment of 'abrí'.

target: Cuando los invitados se despertaron, yo ya había vuelto de nadar en el mar y el café estaba listo.
english: By the time our guests were up, I'd already got back from my swim in the sea and the coffee was ready.
grammar: 'Ya había vuelto' – the past perfect flags the earlier of two past events: the swim ended before the guests woke.

target: De joven viajé mucho por trabajo, pero nunca había venido a esta parte del mundo.
english: When I was younger I travelled a lot for work, but I'd never been to this part of the world.
grammar: 'Nunca había venido' – the pluperfect measures up to a past reference point: no visit before this one began.

target: Llegamos al cine con tiempo de sobra, pero la función ya había empezado: el horario de la página estaba mal.
english: We got to the cinema with plenty of time to spare, but the film had already started: the times on the website were wrong.
grammar: 'Ya había empezado' – the pluperfect alone says before-we-arrived, no extra time phrase needed to order the events.

target: Llegamos corriendo a la parada, pero el último bus ya había salido.
english: We got to the stop at a run, but the last bus had already gone.
grammar: 'Ya había salido' – 'había' + participle marks the earlier of two past events: gone before we arrived.

target: Llegué puntual al dentista, pero la doctora había tenido una urgencia y tuve que esperar casi una hora.
english: I arrived at the dentist's on time, but the doctor had had an emergency and I ended up waiting nearly an hour.
grammar: 'Había tenido' – the pluperfect supplies the backstory: the emergency came first, and the waiting follows from it.

target: Cuando el cliente pidió cambios, yo ya había entregado la versión final, así que acordamos un plazo nuevo.
english: When the client asked for changes I'd already delivered the final version, so we agreed a new deadline.
grammar: Two pasts in order: 'había entregado' happened before 'pidió' – the pluperfect flags the earlier one.

target: Para cuando llegué al establo, ya habían dado de comer a los caballos.
english: By the time I got to the stables, the horses had already been fed.
grammar: 'Ya habían dado' – the past perfect places the feeding before the arriving: the earlier of two pasts.

target: Habíamos quedado en vernos el primer sábado de junio, pero al final movieron el evento para el fin de semana siguiente.
english: We'd arranged to meet on the first Saturday of June, but in the end they moved the event to the following weekend.
grammar: 'Habíamos quedado' – the arrangement sits one step behind the change of plan, so it takes 'habíamos' + participle.

target: Ya habíamos cerrado la puerta con llave cuando me acordé de que el horno seguía prendido.
english: We'd already locked the door when I remembered the oven was still on.
grammar: 'Ya habíamos cerrado' – the pluperfect locks the door before 'me acordé' arrives, keeping the two pasts in order.

target: Salimos a la avenida cuando el desfile ya había pasado y solo quedaba confeti en el suelo.
english: We came out onto the avenue when the parade had already gone by, and there was only confetti left on the ground.
grammar: After the pluperfect 'ya había pasado', the aftermath sits in the imperfect: 'quedaba' paints the leftovers.

target: Corrí hasta el andén, pero el tren ya se había ido, así que me tomé un café mientras esperaba el siguiente.
english: I ran all the way to the platform, but the train had already gone, so I had a coffee while I waited for the next one.
grammar: 'Ya se había ido' – 'ya' plus the pluperfect is the classic too-late note: the going was done before the arriving.

target: Cuando quise reservar el curso de acuarela, ya se habían llenado todos los cupos.
english: By the time I tried to book the watercolour course, all the places had already filled up.
grammar: 'Se habían llenado' – 'habían' + participle places the filling-up before the past attempt 'quise reservar'.

target: Este no es el color que había pedido en línea. ¿Me lo pueden cambiar sin costo?
english: This isn't the colour I'd ordered online – can you exchange it free of charge?
grammar: 'Había pedido' steps a layer further back – the ordering happened before this wrong colour turned up.

target: Conseguí cita con el especialista después de tanto insistir, pero para entonces ya me había recuperado del todo.
english: I got an appointment with the specialist after no end of chasing, but by then I'd already made a full recovery.
grammar: 'Ya me había recuperado' – the past perfect marks the recovery as complete before the appointment arrived.

target: Ya para marzo habíamos gastado casi todo lo que ahorramos en enero.
english: By March we'd already spent nearly everything we saved in January.
grammar: 'Ya para marzo' sets the by-then marker, and 'habíamos gastado' shows the spending complete before that point.

target: Le expliqué al médico que nunca me había dolido tanto la espalda.
english: I explained to the doctor that my back had never hurt this much before.
grammar: 'Nunca me había dolido' – 'había' + participle looks further back than 'expliqué': pain history before the telling.

target: Pedimos una habitación con dos camas, pero al llegar descubrimos que nos habían dado una matrimonial.
english: We asked for a twin room, but when we arrived we found they'd given us a double.
grammar: 'Nos habían dado' – the giving predates the arriving, so it steps one layer back with 'haber' + participle.

target: La feria ya había levantado los puestos cuando llegué a la esquina.
english: The street market had already packed up its stalls by the time I reached the corner.
grammar: 'Ya había levantado los puestos' – 'ya' plus pluperfect is the already-too-late pairing: done before 'llegué'.

target: Regresamos por el sombrero que vimos en la vitrina, pero la tienda ya había bajado la reja.
english: We went back for the hat we'd seen in the window, but the shop had already pulled down the shutter.
grammar: Two layers of past: 'regresamos' is the return, 'había bajado' the shutting that had already beaten it.

target: Nos trajeron pollo, pero nosotras habíamos pedido pescado.
english: They brought us chicken, but we'd ordered fish.
grammar: 'Habíamos pedido' reaches further back than 'trajeron' – the ordering came before the bringing.

target: Para cuando llegamos a Josselin, los huéspedes ya se habían instalado.
english: By the time we arrived at Josselin, the guests had already settled in.
grammar: 'Para cuando llegamos' means by the time we arrived – and the settling in was already done by then.

target: Me detuve a amarrarme el zapato y, cuando alcé la vista, el resto del grupo ya había cruzado.
english: I stopped to tie my shoe, and when I looked up the rest of the group had already crossed.
grammar: 'Había cruzado' – after 'haber' the participle freezes in -o: it never agrees, whoever does the crossing.

target: Al volver del mercado, descubrimos que el viento había tirado dos macetas del balcón.
english: When we got back from the market, we found the wind had knocked two plant pots off the balcony.
grammar: 'El viento había tirado' – 'había' + participle marks damage already done before they got back.

target: Cuando volví al puesto, ya habían vendido las últimas fresas.
english: By the time I got back to the stall, they'd already sold the last of the strawberries.
grammar: 'Ya habían vendido' happened before 'volví' – 'haber' + participle marks the earlier of two pasts.

target: Cuando por fin salté por primera vez, ya había cancelado esa clase dos veces por puros nervios.
english: By the time I finally jumped for the first time, I'd already cancelled that lesson twice out of sheer nerves.
grammar: 'Había' + participle sets the earlier past: 'ya había cancelado' – the cancelling comes before the jump.

target: Cuando subimos a despedirlos, ya habían tendido la cama y doblado las toallas usadas.
english: When we went up to see them off, they'd already made the bed and folded the used towels.
grammar: 'Habían tendido... y doblado' – one 'habían' covers both participles, no need to repeat it before the second.

target: Cuando quise pagar, me di cuenta de que había dejado la billetera en el hotel.
english: When I went to pay, I realised I'd left my purse at the hotel.
grammar: 'Había dejado' – the leaving happened before the noticing, so it steps back a tense with 'haber'.

target: Nos arrepentimos apenas colgamos: habíamos dicho que sí sin mirar bien el calendario.
english: We regretted it as soon as we hung up: we'd said yes without properly checking the calendar.
grammar: 'Habíamos dicho' – the pluperfect jumps behind the story's now: the yes was given before the call ended.

target: Ya había firmado el contrato cuando me fijé en la cláusula del depósito. Por suerte se pudo corregir.
english: I'd already signed the contract when I noticed the deposit clause. Luckily it could be put right.
grammar: 'Ya había firmado' – 'ya' + pluperfect stamps the signing as complete when the noticing arrived.

target: Cuando por fin encontré la calle, me di cuenta de que había entendido mal las indicaciones.
english: When I finally found the street, I realised I'd misunderstood the directions.
grammar: 'Había entendido mal' – the pluperfect sets the misreading before 'encontré': one past tucked behind another.

target: Subimos casi corriendo hasta la iglesia, pero ya habían cerrado la puerta con llave.
english: We practically ran up to the church, but they'd already locked the door.
grammar: 'Ya habían cerrado' – plural 'habían' for the unnamed they: whoever locks up had locked up before us.

target: Habíamos pensado quedarnos una noche más, pero al final decidimos volver con el resto del grupo.
english: We'd thought about staying one more night, but in the end we decided to head back with the rest of the group.
grammar: 'Habíamos pensado' – pluperfect for a plan that predates the past decision: thought first, 'decidimos' after.

target: Resulta que la aerolínea ya nos había cambiado de puerta y nadie avisó nada.
english: It turns out the airline had already changed our gate and nobody said a thing.
grammar: 'Ya nos había cambiado' – the past perfect back-dates the gate switch: done before anyone found out.

target: Cuando por fin salió el sol en septiembre, ya nos habíamos acostumbrado a cargar paraguas a todas partes.
english: When the sun finally came out in September, we'd already got used to carrying an umbrella everywhere.
grammar: 'Ya nos habíamos acostumbrado' – the pluperfect orders two pasts: the getting-used-to came before the sun did.

target: Total que me quedé sin el saco: cuando por fin volví a la tienda, ya lo habían vendido.
english: Anyway, the upshot was I didn't get the jacket: by the time I finally went back to the shop, they'd already sold it.
grammar: 'Ya lo habían vendido' – seen from the return, the selling was already history: the pluperfect keeps that order.

target: Nunca había visto un desfile como el del feriado de mayo, la calle entera se llenó de música.
english: I'd never seen a parade like the one on the May public holiday – the whole street filled with music.
grammar: 'Nunca había visto' – the pluperfect looks back from a past moment: no parade like it up to that very day.

target: Cuando los diplomáticos llegaban a la mesa, Scout ya había redactado el borrador del acuerdo.
english: By the time the diplomats reached the table, Scout had already drafted the agreement.
grammar: 'Ya había redactado' – the pluperfect marks the earlier of two pasts: the drafting beat the arriving.

target: El trámite cerraba en octubre, según yo, pero cuando fui a preguntar ya lo habían cerrado hacía semanas.
english: The application closed in October, or so I thought, but when I went to ask they'd already closed it weeks before.
grammar: 'Hacía semanas' – inside a past story, ago becomes 'hacía' rather than 'hace': weeks counted back from that visit.

target: Cuando entramos al salón, ya habían colgado los adornos y armado casi todas las mesas.
english: When we walked into the hall, they'd already hung the decorations and set up nearly all the tables.
grammar: 'Ya habían colgado' – habían + participle sets the decorating before another past moment: our arrival.

target: Cuando fui a usar la mantequilla, alguien ya se había terminado el último pedazo.
english: When I went to use the butter, someone had already finished off the last bit.
grammar: 'Ya se había terminado' – había + participle reaches back before the main past: gone before I got there.

target: Resulta que el paquete que llevaba semanas esperando había estado todo el tiempo en el correo.
english: It turns out the parcel I'd been waiting weeks for had been sitting at the post office the whole time.
grammar: 'Había estado' – the pluperfect stretches over a whole state: the weeks of sitting all come before the finding-out.

target: El cocinero ya había apagado la cocina cuando llegamos a la una, así que solo quedaban platos fríos.
english: The cook had already shut down the kitchen when we arrived at one, so there were only cold dishes left.
grammar: 'Ya había apagado' – 'había' + participle marks the earlier of two pasts: the kitchen closed before 'llegamos'.

target: Cuando llegué a la playa, las demás ya se habían metido y me hacían señas desde el agua.
english: By the time I got to the beach the others were already in, waving at me from the water.
grammar: The tenses do the sequencing: preterite 'llegué' is the arrival, 'se habían metido' happened before it.

target: Puede que estés en lo cierto. Hasta ahora nadie me lo había planteado así.
english: You may well be right – no one had ever put it to me like that before.
grammar: 'Nadie me lo había planteado' – 'había' + participle marks what had (never) happened before this moment.

target: Quise tomarle una foto al tren, pero cuando saqué el celular ya había pasado.
english: I wanted to get a photo of the train, but by the time I got my phone out it had already gone past.
grammar: 'Ya había pasado' – the pluperfect counts back from a past moment, 'cuando saqué el celular', not from now.

target: Cuando empezó a llover en serio, nosotras ya habíamos salido del agua y estábamos guardando todo.
english: By the time it really started raining we were already out of the water, packing everything up.
grammar: 'Cuando empezó' pins the reference moment, and 'ya habíamos salido' stamps itself earlier than that.

target: Cuando fui a buscar al caballo al campo, ya se había revolcado en el barro y me tocó cepillarlo un buen rato.
english: When I went to fetch the horse from the field he'd already rolled in the mud, so it took me a good while to brush him down.
grammar: 'Ya' loves the pluperfect: 'ya se había revolcado' – the rolling was done before the fetching started.

target: El recibo apareció por fin, pero ya había vencido el plazo para devolver la falda.
english: The receipt finally turned up, but the deadline for returning the skirt had already passed.
grammar: 'Ya había vencido' – 'había' + participle reaches a step further back: the deadline expired before the finding.

target: Ya había pintado media tanda cuando me di cuenta de que el patrón iba al revés.
english: I'd already painted half the batch when I realised the pattern was back to front.
grammar: 'Ya había pintado' – the pluperfect for the act that came first: half the batch was done before 'me di cuenta'.

target: La chaqueta ya había bajado de sesenta a treinta y cinco euros cuando por fin encontré mi talla.
english: The jacket had already come down from sixty to thirty-five euros by the time I finally found my size.
grammar: 'Ya había bajado' – the drop came before the finding, so it sits in the past perfect, one layer under the preterite.

target: El técnico llegó por la tarde, pero para entonces ya habíamos resuelto el problema nosotros mismos.
english: The engineer turned up in the afternoon, but by then we'd already sorted the problem ourselves.
grammar: 'Para entonces' plants a by-then marker – 'ya habíamos resuelto' shows the fixing finished ahead of it.

target: Cuando los historiadores revisaron los códices, Brannagh ya había entrado en la leyenda.
english: By the time historians reviewed the codices, Brannagh had already passed into legend.
grammar: The past perfect steps further back: 'ya había entrado' had already happened before 'revisaron' did.

target: Me di cuenta demasiado tarde de que me había equivocado de fecha: la invitación era para el sábado.
english: I realised too late that I'd got the date wrong: the invitation was for the Saturday.
grammar: 'Me había equivocado' – the mistake happened before the realising did, so it sits one tense further back.

target: Cuando quise corregir el cielo, la pintura ya se había secado, así que el cuadro quedó como estaba.
english: By the time I wanted to fix the sky the paint had already dried, so the painting stayed as it was.
grammar: 'Se había secado' maps onto English one-to-one – 'había' is had, the participle follows: had dried.

target: Cuando quise mostrar la reserva, la aplicación ya se había cerrado sola otra vez.
english: When I tried to show my booking, the app had already crashed again.
grammar: 'Ya se había cerrado' – 'ya' plus the pluperfect: the crash was already complete before 'quise mostrar' happened.

target: Nadie sabe hacia dónde correrá Bear. Ni siquiera Bear lo sabe.
english: Nobody knows which way Bear will run next – not even Bear knows.
grammar: 'hacia dónde correrá' – a real question about the future takes the plain future tense, same as English.

target: ¿De quién será este suéter? Lleva semanas colgado en el perchero de la entrada.
english: Whose jumper can this be? It's been hanging on the hall coat rack for weeks.
grammar: '¿De quién será este suéter?' – the future 'será' wonders about the present: a guess, not a prediction.
