target: La cocina va a quedar preciosa con estos azulejos pintados a mano.
english: The kitchen is going to look lovely with these hand-painted tiles.
grammar: 'Va a quedar' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future, covering plans and predictions alike.

target: Antoine y yo vamos a hacer un viaje juntos a Bolivia.
english: Antoine and I are going to take a trip to Bolivia together.
grammar: Plans use 'ir a' + infinitive: 'vamos a hacer un viaje' – the everyday future, like English going to.

target: Llegamos antes del mediodía. ¿Habrá manera de dejar las maletas mientras alistan la habitación?
english: We've arrived before midday – is there any chance of leaving the cases while the room's being got ready?
grammar: 'Habrá manera' – the future of 'hay' isn't predicting, it asks a polite maybe: might there be a way?

target: Supongo que ya no habrá cupo en el tour de mañana, pero preguntar no cuesta nada.
english: I imagine there are no places left on tomorrow's tour, but there's no harm in asking.
grammar: After 'supongo', the future turns into a guess: 'ya no habrá cupo' – probably none left, not a fixed fact.

target: ¿Dónde diablos se habrá metido Antoine ahora? No le puedo seguir la pista.
english: Where on earth has Antoine gone off to now? I can't keep track.
grammar: 'se habrá metido' – this future form is really a guess about the present: where can he have got to?

target: Me pregunto cómo será Halloween en Nueva York.
english: I wonder what Halloween in New York will be like.
grammar: 'Me pregunto' – to wonder is to ask yourself: reflexive 'preguntarse' plus an indirect question with 'cómo'.

target: A este teclado ya no le funciona la tecla de la a. Tendrá alguna miga metida debajo.
english: The A key on this keyboard has stopped working. There'll be a crumb wedged underneath.
grammar: 'Tendrá' is a hunch, not a forecast – the future tense doubles as Spanish's way of saying probably.

target: Con este tráfico llegaremos justo para el brindis, ni un minuto antes.
english: With this traffic we'll arrive just in time for the toast – not a minute earlier.
grammar: 'Llegaremos' – the future ending sits on the whole infinitive: llegar + -emos, one word, no will needed.

target: Voy a probar un patrón geométrico en la próxima tanda, a ver qué tal sale.
english: I'm going to try a geometric pattern on the next batch and see how it turns out.
grammar: 'Voy a probar' – 'ir a' + infinitive covers plans and intentions, while the -rá future leans towards predictions.

target: Ya estarán por florecer los jacarandás, siempre se adelantan cuando el año viene caluroso.
english: The jacarandas must be about to flower by now – they always come early when the year's been a warm one.
grammar: 'Estarán por florecer' – 'estar por' + infinitive means to be about to: the trees sit on the verge of flowering.

target: Antoine hará los trámites mañana. Mañana, en su calendario, es un concepto flexible.
english: Antoine will do the paperwork tomorrow. Tomorrow, in his calendar, is a flexible concept.
grammar: The bare future 'hará' leans towards prediction – a firm plan would sooner be 'va a hacer'.

target: Me pregunto si el Jaguar nos hará ver como unos creídos.
english: I do wonder whether the Jaguar will make us look like we're full of ourselves.
grammar: 'Me pregunto si' frames a wondering, so the future 'hará' reads as speculation about the present, not a prediction.

target: ¿Adónde habrá ido Ken en la moto? Salió hace un buen rato.
english: Where's Ken got to on the bike? He went out a good while ago.
grammar: 'habrá ido' – the future perfect guesses about the recent past: where can he have got to, not where he will go.

target: En la casita de los pájaros vive alguien: serán herrerillos, me imagino.
english: Something's living in the bird box: blue tits, I'd imagine.
grammar: 'serán herrerillos' – the future used for a guess: probably blue tits, likelihood rather than a forecast.

target: Cuando abro el horno, es como Navidad: nunca sabes qué encontrarás.
english: Opening the kiln is like Christmas – you never know what you'll find.
grammar: 'Encontrarás' – the future is built on the whole infinitive: 'encontrar' plus the ending '-ás'.

target: Este paisaje de Sussex lo voy a regalar en Navidad, aunque todavía no sé a quién.
english: I'm going to give this Sussex landscape away at Christmas, though I don't know who to yet.
grammar: With 'ir a', the pronoun has two homes: 'lo voy a regalar' here, or glued on as 'voy a regalarlo'.

target: ¿Qué hora será allá ahora? Con la diferencia horaria siempre me confundo.
english: What time is it over there now, I wonder? The time difference always trips me up.
grammar: 'Qué hora será' – this future doesn't predict, it wonders: Spanish uses the future tense to guess about now.

target: La cámara del timbre dejó de grabar anoche. Se habrá desconectado del wifi otra vez.
english: The doorbell camera stopped recording last night. It must have lost the wifi again.
grammar: 'Se habrá desconectado' – haber's future plus a participle reads as a must-have guess, not a coming event.

target: Será carísimo llamar a un electricista un domingo, mejor esperamos al lunes.
english: It'll cost a fortune to call an electrician out on a Sunday – better to wait until Monday.
grammar: 'Será carísimo' – the future tense doubles as an educated guess: it's bound to be, surely will be, expensive.

target: La próxima vez haré preguntas sorpresa. Elegantes, pero sorpresa.
english: Next time I'll ask surprise questions. Elegant ones, but surprise ones.
grammar: 'Haré' – hacer's future shrinks the stem to har-, and the endings stay perfectly regular.

target: ¿Se habrá ido la luz en toda la cuadra o nada más en esta casa?
english: Has the power gone off on the whole block, or is it just this house?
grammar: 'Se habrá ido la luz' – 'habrá' + participle turns the future into a wondering guess about right now.

target: ¿Será muy lejos para ir a pie? Con estas maletas no quiero arriesgarme.
english: I wonder if it's too far to walk – with these suitcases I don't want to chance it.
grammar: 'Será muy lejos' – the future here isn't about later, it wonders about the present: might it be far?

target: ¿Cuántos carros antiguos querrá tener Ken? Es una pregunta que prefiero no hacerme.
english: How many vintage cars does Ken want to own? A question I prefer not to ask myself.
grammar: 'querrá' is future in form only – it voices a guess about what Ken currently wants, Spanish's built-in probably.

target: Haremos escala en Bogotá, así que aprovecharé para estirar las piernas y tomar un buen café.
english: We stop over in Bogotá, so I'll make the most of it to stretch my legs and have a decent coffee.
grammar: 'Aprovecharé' is the whole infinitive plus -é – the Spanish future is one word where English needs will.

target: Esta semana las mareas andan raras, así que iremos ajustando la hora del baño día a día.
english: The tides are all over the place this week, so we'll adjust our swim time day by day.
grammar: 'Iremos ajustando' – 'iremos' plus the -ando form means we'll adjust bit by bit, day by day, not in one go.

target: ¿Tiene algo para el mareo? Mañana vamos a cruzar la cordillera en bus.
english: Have you got anything for travel sickness? We're crossing the mountains by bus tomorrow.
grammar: 'Vamos a cruzar' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday future for a plan already made, like going to.

target: ¿Cuándo será el cambio de hora? Todos los años me agarra por sorpresa.
english: When will the clocks be changing? It catches me out every single year.
grammar: 'Cuándo será' – 'será' is the one-word future: Spanish bolts '-á' onto 'ser', no separate word for 'will'.

target: ¿Se verá bien el atardecer hoy? Tenía pensado subir al mirador.
english: Will the sunset be worth seeing today, I wonder? I'd been planning to go up to the viewpoint.
grammar: '¿Se verá bien el atardecer hoy?' – the future tense can wonder aloud: a question asked of nobody in particular.

target: Parece que va a llover toda la tarde, así que mejor lleva paraguas.
english: It looks like it's going to rain all afternoon, so best take an umbrella.
grammar: 'Va a llover' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday future, the natural pick for weather on its way.

target: ¿A cómo estará el kilo de limones en esta época del año?
english: I wonder what a kilo of lemons is going for at this time of year.
grammar: 'Estará' here wonders, not predicts – the future tense is how Spanish muses about a present price.

target: ¿Será que la oficina abre en feriado? Llamaré antes de ir, por si las dudas.
english: I wonder whether the office is open on the bank holiday – I'll ring before going, just to be safe.
grammar: 'Será que' + a question is the future of conjecture – the tense wonders aloud instead of predicting.

target: Van a llegar como a las seis, así que voy a dejar preparado algo de comer por si vienen con hambre del viaje.
english: They'll be arriving around six, so I'm going to leave something ready to eat in case they're hungry from the journey.
grammar: 'Van a llegar' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future: 'llegarán' would sound more formal or written.

target: ¿Habrá mucha fila para desembarcar? Mejor bajamos al carro apenas avisen.
english: I wonder if there'll be a big queue to get off. We'd better go down to the car as soon as they call it.
grammar: 'Habrá' – Spanish wonders with the future tense: a question in the future form muses rather than asks for facts.

target: Habrá algún desvío más adelante, porque todos los carros están girando en esta esquina.
english: There must be a diversion up ahead, because all the cars are turning at this corner.
grammar: 'Habrá algún desvío' – the future used to guess about now: there must be one, going by the traffic.

target: Cada año decimos que habrá que talar el manzano, y cada año le damos otra oportunidad.
english: Every year we say the apple tree will have to come down, and every year we give it one more chance.
grammar: 'Hay que' (one must) also has a future: 'habrá que talar' – it will need doing, doer left unnamed.

target: ¿Saldrá muy caro cambiar esta pantalla rota? A lo mejor conviene más un aparato nuevo.
english: Will it cost a lot to replace this cracked screen, I wonder? It might make more sense to get a new one.
grammar: 'Saldrá muy caro' – asked with the future, the question turns into wondering aloud rather than asking anyone.

target: Mi cumpleaños cae en sábado el año que viene, así que habrá que celebrarlo como se debe.
english: My birthday falls on a Saturday next year, so it'll have to be celebrated properly.
grammar: 'Habrá que celebrarlo' – 'hay que' (one must) in the future: it will have to be done, with no doer named.

target: Habrá llovido de madrugada, porque las calles están empapadas.
english: It must have rained in the early hours – the streets are soaked.
grammar: 'Habrá llovido' – the future perfect guesses about the past: it must have rained, going by the streets.

target: No entendí bien el precio: ¿serán quinientos o quince? Los números todavía se me enredan.
english: I didn't quite catch the price – would that be five hundred or fifteen? I still get in a muddle with numbers.
grammar: 'Serán quinientos' – this future doesn't predict, it wonders about the present: would that be five hundred?

target: Nunca sabemos cuándo va a aparecer el próximo peregrino, pero seguro que llega a la hora de la cena.
english: We never know when the next pilgrim is going to turn up, but you can be sure it'll be at dinnertime.
grammar: Everyday future is 'ir a' + infinitive: 'va a aparecer' – going to turn up, no future ending needed.

target: ¿Estará enojado el del quiosco? Hoy ni me saludó, con lo sonriente que es siempre.
english: Is the man at the kiosk cross with me, I wonder? He didn't even say hello today, and he's usually all smiles.
grammar: 'Estará enojado' – the future tense here wonders about the present: a guess about now, not a claim about later.

target: ¿Le faltará mucho al pollo? Por el olor, yo diría que ya casi está.
english: Can the chicken need much longer? Going by the smell, I'd say it's nearly done.
grammar: 'Le faltará mucho' – the future here guesses about right now: 'faltará' wonders, it doesn't predict.

target: Me pregunto cuándo instalará Antoine su bidé.
english: I wonder when Antoine will install his bidet.
grammar: Accented 'cuándo' asks a real question, so the plain future 'instalará' does the job.

target: ¿Estará abierto el mercado el domingo, o mejor vengo el sábado?
english: Will the market be open on Sunday, I wonder – or should I come on Saturday instead?
grammar: 'Estará' isn't a forecast here – the future tense also wonders: will it be open, I wonder.

target: Vamos a compartir unas entradas mientras decidimos el plato fuerte.
english: We're going to share some starters while we decide on the main course.
grammar: 'Vamos a compartir' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future, like English going to.

target: Cuando ustedes lleguen, yo ya habré hecho las compras.
english: By the time you all get here, I'll have already done the shopping.
grammar: 'Ya habré hecho' – 'habré' + participle is the future perfect: finished before the arriving even happens.

target: No encuentro el cargador por ninguna parte. Lo habré dejado enchufado junto a la cama.
english: I can't find the charger anywhere. I must have left it plugged in by the bed.
grammar: 'Lo habré dejado' – habré + participle turns the future into a best guess about one's own past doings.

target: El altavoz se desconecta a cada rato. Será cosa del bluetooth, que nunca he entendido bien.
english: The speaker keeps cutting out. It'll be something to do with the bluetooth, which I've never properly understood.
grammar: 'Será cosa del bluetooth' – this 'será' guesses about the present, there's no future meaning in it.

target: ¿Cuándo se va a comprar una casa Antoine de una vez?
english: When is Antoine going to buy a house already?
grammar: Buying for yourself is reflexive: 'se va a comprar una casa' – 'comprarse' = buy for oneself.

target: Los vuelos de diciembre van a estar carísimos, así que voy a comprar el boleto con meses de anticipación.
english: Flights in December are going to be sky-high, so I'm going to buy my ticket months in advance.
grammar: 'Voy a comprar' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future, working just like English going to.

target: Mientras haya un partido que comentar, esta familia seguirá unida.
english: As long as there's a match to talk about, this family will stay together.
grammar: 'Seguirá unida' – seguir + adjective means to stay a certain way, and the -á ending puts it in the future.

target: El celular se me descarga rapidísimo. Será que el frío gasta la batería.
english: My phone's draining terribly fast – I suppose the cold wears the battery down.
grammar: 'Será que' opens a hunch about the present: I suppose the cold does it – a guess, not a forecast.

target: Si funciona, con lo del Airbnb pagaremos el mantenimiento de la casa, que no es poco.
english: If it works, the Airbnb money will cover the upkeep of the house, which is no small thing.
grammar: After conditional 'si' Spanish keeps the present – 'Si funciona' – and saves the future for the result: 'pagaremos'.

target: La impresora no imprime nada. Se habrá quedado sin tinta, porque papel sí tiene.
english: The printer isn't printing a thing. It'll have run out of ink – it's certainly got paper.
grammar: 'Se habrá quedado sin tinta' – habrá + participle makes a confident guess about what already happened.

target: El sábado vamos a salir a caballo por los Downs, si el pronóstico no cambia otra vez.
english: On Saturday we're going to hack out on the Downs, as long as the forecast doesn't change again.
grammar: The everyday future is 'ir a' + infinitive: 'vamos a salir' – present-tense 'vamos' doing going-to duty.

target: Mañana tengo una videollamada con el equipo del proyecto, así que voy a dejar mis preguntas preparadas esta noche.
english: Tomorrow I've got a video call with the project team, so I'm going to get my questions ready tonight.
grammar: 'Voy a dejar' – 'ir a' + infinitive is the everyday spoken future for plans, no -é ending needed.

target: ¿Cuánto costará la entrada? Por si acaso, voy a sacar más plata.
english: How much will the entrance fee be, I wonder? I'll get some more cash out just in case.
grammar: 'Costará' is a guess, not a forecast – Spanish borrows the future tense for I wonder how much.

target: Supongo que para agosto ya sabremos si nos aprobaron el crédito, esas cosas siempre demoran meses.
english: I imagine by August we'll know whether they've approved the loan – that sort of thing always takes months.
grammar: 'Ya sabremos' – the plain future, with 'saber' shrinking to 'sabr-' before the ending: irregular stem, regular tail.

target: Este esmalte se ve gris ahora, pero quedará azul después de la cocción.
english: This glaze looks grey now, but it'll come out blue after firing.
grammar: 'Quedará' – infinitive + '-á' forms the simple future, the tense of predictions rather than plans.

target: El vuelo sale a las seis y cuarto de la mañana, así que vamos a pedir el taxi desde la noche anterior.
english: The flight leaves at a quarter past six in the morning, so we're going to book the taxi the night before.
grammar: 'El vuelo sale' – timetabled departures use the plain present: the schedule is fixed, so no future tense is needed.

target: El mes que viene iremos a un concierto en el Barbican.
english: Next month we'll go to a concert at the Barbican.
grammar: 'Iremos' – even ir, irregular nearly everywhere, builds its future by the rule: infinitive plus -emos.

target: Yo tendría que haber preguntado el precio antes, pero me dio pena y terminé pagando de más.
english: I should have asked the price first, but I was too embarrassed and ended up paying over the odds.
grammar: 'Tendría que haber preguntado' – conditional 'tener que' + 'haber' + participle is Spanish for should have done.

target: Yo no aceptaría un encargo urgente para el fin de semana sin cobrar una tarifa extra.
english: I wouldn't take on an urgent weekend job without charging a rush fee.
grammar: 'No aceptaría' – wouldn't take it on: the -ría ending keeps it hypothetical, no real job is on the table.

target: Habría que pintar las rejas antes de que se oxiden más.
english: The railings could do with painting before they rust any further.
grammar: 'Habría que' is 'hay que' (one must) gone conditional – an impersonal ought, aimed at nobody in particular.

target: Me habría gustado empezar con el español mucho antes, pero más vale tarde que nunca.
english: I'd have liked to start on Spanish much sooner, but better late than never.
grammar: 'Me habría gustado' – gustar's conditional perfect: 'habría' + participle for a start that never happened.

target: Debería limpiar los pinceles apenas termino, pero casi siempre lo dejo para el día siguiente.
english: I ought to clean my brushes the minute I finish, but I almost always leave it till the next day.
grammar: 'Debería limpiar' – conditional 'deber' reproaches gently: ought to, softer than a flat 'debo'.

target: Yo que tú, cambiaría solo un poco aquí. En el centro pagan mejor.
english: If I were you I'd only change a little here – you get a better rate in town.
grammar: 'Yo que tú' is if I were you with no verb at all – 'cambiaría' then advises in the conditional.

target: ¿Usted qué me aconsejaría, llevo el carro o me muevo en tren?
english: What would you advise, shall I take the car or just use the trains?
grammar: 'Aconsejaría' – the conditional turns a request for advice polite: what would you advise, softer than the present.

target: Yo diría que aprender a caerse sin lastimarse es tan importante como aprender a montar.
english: I'd say learning to fall without hurting yourself is just as important as learning to ride.
grammar: 'Yo diría que' softens the claim with the conditional – I'd say, an opinion offered rather than declared.

target: Yo que tú, escucharía la radio en español mientras cocinas, el oído se acostumbra solo.
english: If I were you I'd have the radio on in Spanish while you cook, your ear tunes in by itself.
grammar: 'Yo que tú' squeezes if I were you into three words, then the advice runs on conditional 'escucharía'.

target: Habría sido mejor reservar con anticipación, porque a última hora todo estaba carísimo.
english: It would have been better to book ahead, because at the last minute everything was terribly expensive.
grammar: 'Habría sido mejor' + infinitive – the conditional perfect hands out hindsight verdicts on chances already gone.

target: Yo le pediría al peluquero algo más corto, con este calor se agradece.
english: I'd ask the hairdresser for something shorter – in this heat you'll be glad of it.
grammar: 'Yo le pediría' – conditional '-ría' softens advice into what-I-would-do rather than what you should do.

target: Estas chirimoyas son una delicia. En casa jamás encontraría fruta tan dulce.
english: These custard apples are a delight – I'd never find fruit this sweet back home.
grammar: 'Jamás encontraría' – the conditional imagines the hunt back home: would never find, hypothetically.

target: De más joven habría dicho que no a un viaje así. Ahora digo que sí primero y después veo cómo lo resuelvo.
english: When I was younger I'd have said no to a trip like that. Now I say yes first and work out the details afterwards.
grammar: 'De más joven habría dicho' – a time phrase alone frames the hypothetical, no 'si' clause needed.

target: Cualquier ministro de economía haría bien en pasar una tarde con Pierre.
english: Any finance minister would do well to spend an afternoon with Pierre.
grammar: 'Haría bien en' – would do well to: the conditional of hacer, and the idiom brings its own 'en'.

target: Ningún jeque podría pagar lo que vale Brannagh, y lo saben.
english: No sheikh could pay what Brannagh is worth, and they know it.
grammar: 'Podría pagar' – could pay, in theory: the conditional of 'poder' imagines it, nobody is actually paying.

target: Sin Scout, la Guerra Fría habría durado veinte años más.
english: Without Scout, the Cold War would have lasted twenty years longer.
grammar: 'Habría durado' – 'habría' + participle builds would have, the shape of an alternative past.

target: ¿Sería mucha molestia cambiar las papas por ensalada?
english: Would it be too much trouble to swap the chips for a salad?
grammar: 'Sería mucha molestia' floats the request as a mere hypothesis – politer than asking with a flat 'es'.

target: Me caí bajando del bus y tengo el tobillo hinchado. ¿Usted cree que debería hacerme una radiografía?
english: I fell getting off the bus and my ankle's swollen – do you think I ought to have an X-ray?
grammar: 'Debería hacerme una radiografía' – 'deber' in the conditional asks for advice: should I, softer than 'debo'.

target: Yo en tu lugar compraría un buen cuchillo antes que diez aparatos, rinde mucho más.
english: If I were you I'd buy one good knife rather than ten gadgets – you get far more use out of it.
grammar: 'Yo en tu lugar compraría' – the conditional carries advice: what I would do in your place, politely unreal.

target: Yo que tú llevaría un abrigo de todos modos, en la costa el viento engaña.
english: If I were you I'd take a coat anyway – on the coast the wind is deceptive.
grammar: 'Yo que tú' packs if-I-were-you into three words – no verb in it, the conditional 'llevaría' does the imagining.

target: Tenemos una vida repartida entre dos países, y no la cambiaríamos por nada.
english: We have a life split between two countries, and we wouldn't change it for anything.
grammar: 'No la cambiaríamos' – the conditional keeps the swap imaginary: would, not will.

target: A Gary le encanta leer el Daily Mail, aunque ya debería saber que no le conviene.
english: Gary loves reading the Daily Mail, though by now he really should know better.
grammar: Should is 'debería' – 'deber' (must) in the conditional: 'ya debería saber' = he should know by now.

target: Menos mal que Antoine nunca llegó a jugar GTA VI. Le habría arruinado la vida.
english: Thank goodness Antoine never got to play GTA VI. It would have ruined his life.
grammar: 'Le habría arruinado' – the conditional perfect tells the outcome of a past that never took place.

target: Yo dejaría reposar la masa una media hora, así después se estira sin problema.
english: I'd let the dough rest half an hour or so, then it rolls out with no fuss.
grammar: 'Dejaría reposar' – 'dejar' + bare infinitive means to let something do it: no word links the two verbs.

target: ¿Podría dejarme en la esquina? Así no tiene que meterse por esa calle tan angosta.
english: Could you drop me at the corner? That way you don't have to turn into that narrow street.
grammar: '¿Podría dejarme en la esquina?' – 'poder' in the conditional turns can you into a polite could you.

target: Sin el ferry, esta vida entre dos países sería mucho más complicada.
english: Without the ferry, this life between two countries would be a lot more complicated.
grammar: 'Sería' is conditional – 'sin el ferry' packs a whole if-clause into three words, and the tense answers the what-if.

target: Yo en tu caso hablaría directamente con la dueña de la casa, con la agencia todo se demora el doble.
english: In your shoes I'd speak to the owner of the house directly, everything takes twice as long through the agency.
grammar: 'Yo en tu caso' sets up the in-your-shoes swap, and the advice lands in conditional 'hablaría'.

target: Pierre sería un guía histórico excelente: hasta sabe reparar audioguías (bueno, no exactamente).
english: Pierre would make an excellent historical guide – he even knows how to repair audioguides (not really).
grammar: 'Hasta sabe' – this 'hasta' means even, not until: he even knows how to fix them.

target: Cualquiera diría que Swansea fue diseñada por los mismos ángeles.
english: You'd think Swansea had been designed by the angels themselves.
grammar: 'Cualquiera diría' – the conditional supposes a typical observer: anyone would say it, nobody actually has.

target: Con un buen ejemplo lo habría entendido a la primera, pero la explicación fue pura teoría.
english: With one good example I'd have understood it straight away, but the explanation was all theory.
grammar: 'Lo habría entendido' – 'habría' + participle is the conditional perfect: how the past would have gone.

target: Te convendría respaldar las fotos del celular de vez en cuando, se pierden más fácil de lo que parece.
english: You'd do well to back up the photos on your phone now and then, they get lost more easily than you'd think.
grammar: 'Te convendría' means it would suit you – note the extra d: 'convenir' turns into 'convendr-' in the conditional.

target: Deberíamos turnarnos para hablar en las llamadas de grupo, cuando hablamos todos a la vez no se entiende nada.
english: We should take turns talking on the group calls, when we all speak at once you can't make anything out.
grammar: 'Deberíamos' – the conditional of 'deber' softens 'we must' into 'we ought to', a suggestion rather than an order.

target: ¿Tú qué harías en mi lugar: reservar de una vez o esperar a que baje el precio?
english: What would you do in my position – book straight away, or wait for the price to drop?
grammar: The conditional asks the hypothetical: 'qué harías en mi lugar' – what would you do, not what will you.

target: Yo le regalaría algo hecho a mano, la gente lo agradece más que cualquier cosa comprada.
english: I'd give them something handmade, people appreciate it far more than anything shop-bought.
grammar: 'Yo le regalaría' – the conditional offers advice as what I would do, gentler than telling anyone what to buy.

target: Al guiso yo le pondría menos cebolla, así no tapa el resto de los sabores.
english: I'd put less onion in the stew – that way it doesn't drown out the other flavours.
grammar: 'Le pondría' – the conditional floats the idea as what I'd do, a suggestion rather than an instruction.

target: Deberíamos haber salido más temprano: con tanto tráfico, tardamos el doble.
english: We should have left earlier: with all that traffic, it took us twice as long.
grammar: 'Deberíamos haber salido' – should have is conditional 'deber' + 'haber' + participle: the regret sits on 'deber'.

target: Cualquiera se pondría nervioso hablando en público, a mí me temblaría hasta la voz.
english: Anyone would get nervous speaking in public – even my voice would shake.
grammar: 'Cualquiera se pondría nervioso' – the '-ría' ending keeps it hypothetical: nobody is actually on stage yet.

target: Eso habría que consultárselo a un ingeniero, a ver si la pared aguanta el peso de otro piso.
english: That's one to ask an engineer – whether the wall can take the weight of another storey.
grammar: 'Habría que' is the conditional of 'hay que' – someone would have to ask, advice floated with no one named.

target: ¿Les molestaría cerrar el portón cuando salgan? El viento lo golpea toda la noche.
english: Would you mind shutting the gate when you go out? The wind bangs it all night long.
grammar: 'Les molestaría' – the conditional turns a request into a courtesy: 'would it bother you', hypothetical on purpose.

target: Podría pasarme la tarde entera decorando una sola pieza, el tiempo se me va sin sentir.
english: I could spend a whole afternoon decorating a single piece, the time just slips away.
grammar: 'Podría pasarme' – I could easily spend it: the conditional floats a possibility, nothing is actually planned.

target: Sin el tren directo, iríamos a Londres mucho menos.
english: Without the direct train, we'd go to London far less.
grammar: A phrase can stand in for an if-clause: 'sin el tren directo' sets the condition, so 'iríamos' goes conditional.

target: Con esa paciencia que tienes para explicar, serías muy buena maestra.
english: With that patience you have for explaining things, you'd make a very good teacher.
grammar: 'Serías muy buena maestra' – conditional 'serías' imagines the whole career: would-be, nothing of it real yet.

target: Yo compraría las botas buenas de una vez, porque a la larga las baratas salen más caras.
english: I'd buy the good boots straight away, because in the long run the cheap ones work out dearer.
grammar: 'Yo compraría' – the conditional offers what I would do: advice given without giving an order.

target: Sin los bomberos, el incendio habría alcanzado las casas vecinas en cuestión de minutos.
english: Without the firefighters, the fire would have reached the neighbouring houses in a matter of minutes.
grammar: 'Habría alcanzado' – conditional 'habría' plus participle looks back at what would have happened but never did.

target: Algunos dirían que Antoine procrastina, pero él no estaría de acuerdo.
english: Some would call it procrastination when Antoine puts things off, but he would disagree.
grammar: The conditional hedges: 'dirían' = some would say, and 'no estaría de acuerdo' = he'd disagree.

target: Me quedaría una noche más si no les complica. Anuncian paro de buses para mañana.
english: I'd stay an extra night if it's no trouble – they're announcing a bus strike for tomorrow.
grammar: 'Me quedaría' – the conditional floats the extra night as a possibility, politely leaving the decision open.

target: Sin el grupo, más de un día gris me quedaría en la cama, por eso nos avisamos todas la noche anterior.
english: Without the group I'd stay in bed on more than one grey day, which is why we all message each other the night before.
grammar: 'Sin el grupo' hides an if-clause, so the conditional follows: 'me quedaría' – I would stay put.

target: Según la página, mi pedido debería haber llegado hace tres días y sigue sin aparecer.
english: According to the website, my order should have arrived three days ago and there's still no sign of it.
grammar: 'Debería haber llegado' – conditional 'debería' + 'haber' + participle: a should that has already been missed.

target: ¿De dónde es usted? Por el acento diría que no es de aquí.
english: Where are you from? Going by your accent, I'd say you're not from round here.
grammar: 'Diría' – the conditional turns a claim into a guess: I'd-say, offered with room to be wrong.

target: Con este viento, yo no colgaría la ropa afuera. Se te va a volar toda.
english: With this wind I wouldn't hang the washing outside – it'll all blow away on you.
grammar: 'Yo no colgaría' – the conditional gives advice by imagining yourself in their shoes: I wouldn't.

target: Habría que arreglar el baño de abajo antes de recibir al primer huésped.
english: We'd have to sort out the downstairs bathroom before taking our first guest.
grammar: 'Habría que' – 'hay que' in the conditional: an impersonal we'd-have-to that names no particular doer.

target: Te convendría descargar los mapas antes de salir. En la montaña no vas a tener señal.
english: You'd do well to download the maps before setting off – you won't get any signal in the mountains.
grammar: 'Te convendría' – 'convenir' in the conditional gives gentle advice: it-would-suit-you, softer than a command.

target: ¿Cuánto me cobraría por la caja entera de duraznos?
english: How much would you charge me for the whole box of peaches?
grammar: The conditional softens the ask – 'cobraría' floats would you charge, gentler than a flat 'cobra'.

target: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar un poco la música? Casi no podemos conversar.
english: Would you be so kind as to turn the music down a little? We can barely hold a conversation.
grammar: 'Sería tan amable de' – the conditional dials the request up to full courtesy, a notch above '¿podría?'.

target: Yo compraría el café en grano, molido pierde el aroma a los pocos días.
english: I'd buy the coffee as whole beans, once it's ground it loses its aroma within days.
grammar: 'Compraría' – the conditional builds on the whole infinitive: 'comprar' + -ía, the same endings for every verb.

target: Con más luz, este cuarto sería perfecto para pintar por las tardes.
english: With more light, this room would be perfect for painting in the afternoons.
grammar: 'Con más luz' packs the whole if-clause into three words – the conditional 'sería' does the imagining.

target: Yo en tu lugar despacharía la mochila grande en vez de pelear por espacio en la cabina.
english: If I were you I'd check the big rucksack in rather than fight for cabin space.
grammar: 'Yo en tu lugar despacharía' – if-I-were-you advice runs on the conditional, no si-clause needed.

target: En mi club de lectura aceptarían a Trump. Imagínate las discusiones.
english: Trump would be accepted as a member of my book club – imagine the discussions.
grammar: 'Aceptarían' – they would accept him: the -ían ending keeps it imaginary, and the 'if' is left unsaid.

target: Habría que inventar un premio a la seguridad sin fundamento, y dárselo a Gilles.
english: Someone should invent a prize for unfounded confidence, and give it to Gilles.
grammar: 'Habría que' is 'hay que' (one must) in the conditional – someone ought to, and nobody in particular is named.

target: Nadie lo diría al verla, pero Béa llega a la oficina con techno a todo volumen.
english: You'd never guess it to look at her, but Béa arrives at the office with techno at full blast.
grammar: 'Nadie lo diría' hedges with the conditional – nobody would say so, going only on appearances.
ttsText: Nadie lo diría al verla, pero Bea llega a la oficina con techno a todo volumen.

target: ¿Habría manera de pasar mi cita con el oculista para el jueves a primera hora?
english: Would there be any way of moving my optician's appointment to first thing on Thursday?
grammar: 'Habría manera' – the conditional of 'hay' floats the request gently, softer than a flat 'hay manera'.

target: Deberías subir por el lado de la sombra, es un poco más largo pero se agradece.
english: You should go up on the shady side – it's a little longer but you'll be glad of it.
grammar: 'Deberías subir' – 'deber' in the conditional makes should: softer than 'debes', which is you must.

target: Daría cualquier cosa por saber cómo consigue el cocinero que el arroz quede tan suelto.
english: I'd give anything to know how the cook gets the rice to come out so fluffy.
grammar: 'Daría cualquier cosa' – conditional 'daría' keeps the offer hypothetical: nothing changes hands, it signals longing.

target: Ese papeleo yo no lo dejaría para diciembre, en esas fechas todo se pone más lento.
english: I wouldn't leave that paperwork until December – everything slows down around then.
grammar: 'No lo dejaría' – conditional '-ría' frames advice as what I would (or wouldn't) do, if it were my paperwork.

target: Antes de comprar una casa vieja, yo pediría un informe completo del techo y de la humedad.
english: Before buying an old house I'd ask for a proper report on the roof and the damp.
grammar: 'Yo pediría' – the conditional keeps pedir's infinitive intact, even though the verb's stem bends in other tenses.

target: Esas fotos yo las guardaría también en otra parte. Con las computadoras nunca se sabe.
english: I'd keep those photos somewhere else as well. You never know with computers.
grammar: 'Yo las guardaría' – conditional advice: what I would do in your shoes, gentler than telling you to.

target: Con lo que cuesta estacionar en el centro, saldría más barato ir en tren: son cuatro libras con veinte ida y vuelta.
english: With what parking in town costs, it would work out cheaper to go by train: it's four pounds twenty return.
grammar: 'Saldría más barato' – the conditional weighs an option not taken: what the train would cost if you chose it.

target: Otros cachorros perseguirían la pelota. Twig persigue un futuro mejor para todos.
english: Other puppies would chase the ball; Twig chases a better future for us all.
grammar: 'Perseguirían' – the conditional for what others would do, set against the plain present 'persigue'.

target: ¿Podría escribírmelo? Me sería mucho más fácil buscarlo después.
english: Could you write it down for me? It would be much easier for me to look up later.
grammar: '¿Podría escribírmelo?' – 'poder' in the conditional makes the polite could-you: a request, not a doubt about ability.

target: ¿Qué me aconsejarías ver si solo me queda una mañana libre en la ciudad?
english: What would you advise me to see if I've only got one free morning in the city?
grammar: 'Aconsejarías ver' – 'aconsejar' takes a bare infinitive for the advised action, no 'a' or 'que' in between.

target: ¿Le importaría llegar un poco antes para ayudarme a recibir a la gente?
english: Would you mind arriving a little early to help me welcome people?
grammar: 'Le importaría' – the conditional softens the ask into would-you-mind, gentler than present 'le importa'.

target: ¿Conoces a alguien que arregle goteras? Cada vez que llueve entra agua por el techo.
english: Do you know anyone who fixes leaks? Every time it rains, water gets in through the roof.
grammar: 'Alguien que arregle goteras' – the fixer may not exist, so the verb goes subjunctive, not 'arregla'.

target: Ando buscando un camino al parque que no sea pura cuesta, con este calor no rindo.
english: I'm after a way to the park that isn't all uphill – in this heat I'm good for nothing.
grammar: 'Que no sea pura cuesta' – 'sea' goes subjunctive: the path is wished-for, not one anyone has found yet.

target: Es normal que cada hornada salga un poco distinta, así que nunca prometo un color exacto.
english: It's normal for every firing to come out slightly different, so I never promise an exact colour.
grammar: 'Es normal que' still takes the subjunctive: 'salga', not 'sale' – value judgements do this even with routine facts.

target: ¿Qué me recomienda que no pique tanto?
english: What would you recommend that isn't too spicy?
grammar: 'Que no pique tanto' is subjunctive – you describe a dish you hope for, not one you know exists.

target: Lograr que todos sigan las reglas del club de lectura no es poca cosa.
english: Getting everyone to follow the rules in book club is no small feat.
grammar: 'Lograr que' (to get people to do something) needs the subjunctive: 'que todos sigan las reglas'.

target: Hace falta que alguien acompañe a PapyLou a la misa de gallo cada año, y la verdad es que nadie quiere ir.
english: Somebody has to go with PapyLou to midnight mass every year, and the truth is nobody really wants to.
grammar: Needing something done takes the subjunctive: 'hace falta que alguien acompañe' – wished for, not yet real.

target: Hay palabras que no tienen traducción exacta, y está bien que así sea.
english: Some words have no exact translation, and it's fine that way.
grammar: 'Está bien que así sea' – a verdict on how things are flips the verb to subjunctive: 'sea', not 'es'.

target: Necesito un chip con datos que funcione en varios países, porque el mes que viene cruzo dos fronteras.
english: I need a SIM with data that works in several countries – next month I'm crossing two borders.
grammar: 'Que funcione' is subjunctive – the SIM is wished-for, not found. A real one in hand would take 'funciona'.

target: Te sugiero que apuntes cada mezcla de esmalte en un cuaderno, después una no se acuerda de las proporciones.
english: I suggest you note every glaze mix down in a notebook, you never remember the proportions afterwards.
grammar: 'Te sugiero que apuntes' – suggesting someone else's action sends the 'que' clause into subjunctive: 'apuntes'.

target: Me molesta que la gente se cuele en la fila, pero respiro hondo y lo dejo pasar.
english: It annoys me when people jump the queue, but I take a deep breath and let it go.
grammar: 'Me molesta que la gente se cuele' – annoyance is an emotion trigger, so after 'que' the verb goes subjunctive.

target: No hace falta que riegues el romero todos los días, se da mejor cuando lo dejas tranquilo.
english: There's no need to water the rosemary every day, it does better when you leave it be.
grammar: 'No hace falta que riegues' – talk of what's needed, or not needed, turns the verb to 'riegues', not 'riegas'.

target: Espero que vengan todos los que confirmaron, porque encargamos comida de sobra.
english: I hope everyone who confirmed turns up, because we've ordered food to spare.
grammar: 'Espero que vengan' – hope offers no guarantee, so the hoped-for verb goes subjunctive: 'vengan', not 'vienen'.

target: Me preocupa que se nos haga de noche en plena carretera de montaña.
english: I'm worried we'll be caught out by nightfall on the mountain road.
grammar: Emotion verbs trigger the subjunctive: 'me preocupa que se nos haga de noche' – so 'haga', never 'hace'.

target: Prefiero que me cobren en moneda local y no en dólares.
english: I'd rather you charged me in local currency, not dollars.
grammar: 'Prefiero que' hands the deed to someone else, so the verb goes subjunctive: 'me cobren'.

target: No quiero que la gente piense que somos una familia insoportable solo por el carro.
english: I don't want people thinking we're an insufferable family just because of the car.
grammar: 'quiero que' pushes the verb to 'piense', not 'piensa' – yet the inner belief 'que somos' stays plain indicative.

target: Es mejor que crucen un día entre semana, los fines de semana el puerto es un caos.
english: You're better off crossing on a weekday, at weekends the port is chaos.
grammar: 'Es mejor que crucen' – 'es mejor que' passes a judgement, and judgements push the next verb into subjunctive.

target: Yo no diría que sea caro. Comparado con lo que pagamos en Europa, es una ganga.
english: I wouldn't say it's expensive – compared with what we pay in Europe, it's a bargain.
grammar: Denying an opinion triggers the subjunctive: 'no diría que sea caro' – a plain claim would use 'es'.

target: No creo que alcancemos a llegar antes de que cierren la boletería.
english: I don't think we'll make it before the ticket office closes.
grammar: 'No creo que' adds doubt, and doubt changes the verb: 'alcancemos' where plain 'creo que' would keep 'alcanzamos'.

target: Me sorprende que se ofenda por tan poca cosa, normalmente es de lo más tranquilo.
english: It surprises me that he takes offence at such small things – normally he's really easy-going.
grammar: 'Me sorprende que se ofenda' – surprise is an emotion trigger too, and even a true fact takes subjunctive after it.

target: Busco un esmalte que no sea tan brillante, algo más mate para las puertas.
english: I'm looking for a paint that's not so glossy – something more matt for the doors.
grammar: 'Que no sea tan brillante' – subjunctive 'sea' because this is the paint you're after, not one you've actually found.

target: Mi consejo es que empieces con un caballo tranquilo hasta que agarres confianza.
english: My advice is to start with a calm horse until you get your confidence up.
grammar: 'Mi consejo es que empieces' – advice aimed at another person's action takes subjunctive, so 'empieces', not 'empiezas'.

target: Espero que la masa suba, la dejé cerca de la ventana donde da el sol.
english: I hope the dough rises – I left it near the window where the sun comes in.
grammar: Hoping triggers the subjunctive: 'espero que la masa suba', not 'sube' – the rise is wished for, not certain.

target: Ojalá te toque un profesor paciente, porque al principio uno pregunta lo mismo mil veces.
english: Let's hope you get a patient teacher, because at the start you ask the same thing a thousand times.
grammar: 'Ojalá te toque' – 'ojalá' comes from Arabic (God willing) and always pulls the verb into the subjunctive.

target: Para que te acepten en Latour de France, es necesario que tu bisabuelo haya nacido allí.
english: To be accepted in Latour de France, your great-grandfather needs to have been born there.
grammar: 'Es necesario que' opens the subjunctive – 'haya nacido', its perfect form, for a deed already done.

target: Me alegra que la fecha les sirva a todos, no era nada fácil cuadrar tantas agendas.
english: I'm glad the date works for everyone – it was no easy job squaring so many diaries.
grammar: 'Me alegra que' runs on emotion, and emotion about a fact still takes subjunctive – 'sirva', not 'sirve'.

target: Me encanta que casi todos los pueblos tengan una iglesia de piedra con siglos de historia.
english: I love that almost every village has a stone church with centuries of history.
grammar: Even a true fact turns subjunctive after 'me encanta que' – feeling, not doubt, is what flips 'tengan'.

target: En este oficio es fundamental que el lector no note que hubo un original en otro idioma.
english: In this trade it's essential that the reader doesn't notice there was ever an original in another language.
grammar: 'Que el lector no note' – after 'es fundamental que' the verb turns subjunctive: 'note', not 'nota'.

target: Soy alérgica a la penicilina, así que hace falta que me receten otro antibiótico.
english: I'm allergic to penicillin, so they'll have to prescribe me a different antibiotic.
grammar: 'Hace falta que' states a need, and needs take the subjunctive: 'me receten', not 'me recetan'.

target: Es importante que el marco no compita con el cuadro: casi siempre elijo el más sencillo.
english: It's important that the frame doesn't compete with the painting: I almost always choose the simplest one.
grammar: 'Es importante que' passes judgement rather than reporting fact, so 'compita' goes subjunctive.

target: Ojalá no haga tanto calor mañana, porque vamos a caminar bastante.
english: I hope it's not so hot tomorrow, because we'll be doing a fair bit of walking.
grammar: 'Ojalá' always takes the subjunctive: 'no haga tanto calor' – a hope, so 'haga', never 'hace'.

target: Queremos que sea una sorpresa, así que no vayas a comentar nada en el grupo.
english: We want it to be a surprise, so don't go mentioning anything in the group chat.
grammar: 'Queremos que sea' – when the wanting and the doing belong to different subjects, the verb goes subjunctive.

target: Me alegra que seas tan sincera conmigo, aunque a veces la verdad duela un poco.
english: I'm glad you're so honest with me, even if the truth stings a little at times.
grammar: 'Me alegra que seas' – emotion about someone else's behaviour pushes the verb after 'que' to subjunctive 'seas'.

target: Me preocupa que la derecha radical esté ganando terreno en Europa.
english: It worries me that the far right is gaining ground in Europe.
grammar: 'Me preocupa que' reacts with feeling, and feeling switches the verb: 'esté', not 'está'.

target: Sé que no es culpa suya, pero necesito que esto quede resuelto antes del viernes.
english: I know it's not your fault, but I need this sorted out before Friday.
grammar: 'Necesito que' hands the job to someone else, so the verb turns subjunctive: 'quede', not 'queda'.

target: Siempre busco que la visita incluya una galería y un buen almuerzo.
english: I always make sure the trip includes a gallery and a good lunch.
grammar: Aiming at an outcome takes the subjunctive: 'busco que la visita incluya' – wished for, not yet a fact.

target: Yo siempre le pido al taxista que use el taxímetro en vez de inventarse una tarifa.
english: I always ask the driver to use the meter rather than make up a fare.
grammar: A request bends the next verb into subjunctive: 'que use el taxímetro' – 'use', not the plain 'usa'.

target: No es que esté en desacuerdo, es que me faltan datos para opinar con seguridad.
english: It's not that I disagree – I just don't know enough to have a firm view.
grammar: 'No es que esté en desacuerdo' – 'no es que' denies a reason, so its verb turns subjunctive: 'esté'.

target: Solo pido que pare de llover antes de la noche, la idea es poner las mesas afuera.
english: All I ask is that it stops raining before this evening – the idea is to put the tables outside.
grammar: 'Pido que pare' – a request hands the action to someone else, and that hand-over triggers subjunctive 'pare'.

target: Tampoco es que sea terca: es que necesito entender el porqué antes de cambiar de opinión.
english: It's not that I'm stubborn – I just need to understand why before I'll change my mind.
grammar: 'Tampoco es que sea terca' – rejecting an idea turns its verb to 'sea', not 'es': the stubbornness is denied.

target: ¿Le importa que sigamos en español? Sé que es más lento, pero necesito practicar.
english: Do you mind if we stick to Spanish? I know it's slower, but I need the practice.
grammar: 'Le importa que sigamos' – a feeling about an action triggers the subjunctive: 'sigamos', not 'seguimos'.

target: Todavía busco un carpintero que haga puertas a la medida y no cobre una fortuna.
english: I'm still looking for a carpenter who makes made-to-measure doors and doesn't charge a fortune.
grammar: 'Haga' is subjunctive – 'busco un carpintero que haga' hunts for a type of carpenter, not one that's been found.

target: Es fundamental que Twig duerma bien: el mundo libre depende de él.
english: It's essential that Twig sleeps well – the free world depends on him.
grammar: 'Es fundamental que' passes judgement, so the sleeping goes subjunctive – 'duerma', not 'duerme'.

target: Si quieren cenar ahí un sábado, les recomiendo que reserven con varios días de anticipación.
english: If you want to have dinner there on a Saturday, I'd recommend booking several days ahead.
grammar: 'Reserven' is the ustedes subjunctive – LatAm Spanish addresses any group as ustedes, so no 'reservéis' here.

target: Ken quiere que pongamos reglas claras desde el principio: nada de fiestas y respeto por el jardín.
english: Ken wants us to set clear rules from the start: no parties, and respect for the garden.
grammar: Wanting someone else to act triggers the subjunctive: 'quiere que pongamos', never 'ponemos'.

target: No decimos que Floppy haya resucitado, solo decimos que nunca encontramos el cuerpo.
english: We're not saying Floppy rose again – we're just saying we never found the body.
grammar: 'No decimos que' backs away from a claim, so 'haya resucitado' replaces the plain 'ha resucitado'.

target: Conviene que reservemos el ferry con tiempo porque en verano se llena rapidísimo.
english: It's worth booking the ferry well ahead because it fills up fast in summer.
grammar: 'Conviene que' recommends rather than reports, so booking becomes 'reservemos', not 'reservamos'.

target: Me preocupa que algunos vengan al club de lectura sin haber abierto el libro.
english: It worries me that some people come to book club without having opened the book.
grammar: 'Vengan' – the subjunctive is built on the yo form 'vengo', which is where its g comes from.

target: ¿Puede pedirle a la cocina que me prepare algo liviano? A esta hora la comida pesada ya no me cae bien.
english: Could you ask the kitchen to make me something light? Heavy food doesn't agree with me this late.
grammar: 'Que me prepare' – what you ask of the kitchen is a wish, not a fact, so 'preparar' bends to 'prepare'.

target: ¿Habrá algún asiento que esté del lado del pasillo? En los vuelos me levanto seguido.
english: Might there be a seat on the aisle side? I'm up and down a lot on flights.
grammar: 'Algún asiento que esté' – the seat is only hoped for, so its clause takes subjunctive 'esté', not 'está'.

target: Quiero que se sientan como en su casa: agarren lo que necesiten de la cocina sin pedir permiso.
english: I want you to feel at home – help yourselves to whatever you need from the kitchen, no need to ask.
grammar: 'Quiero que se sientan' – wanting someone else to do something sends that second verb into the subjunctive.

target: Creo que es importante que mis hijos reciban educación religiosa en la primaria.
english: I believe it's important for my kids to receive a religious education at primary school.
grammar: Value judgements trigger the subjunctive: 'es importante que' makes it 'reciban', not 'reciben'.

target: Ando buscando una planta que aguante la sombra y el viento, ¿cuál me recomienda?
english: I'm after a plant that can cope with shade and wind, which would you recommend?
grammar: 'Que aguante' – a plant still being searched for gets subjunctive in its description: 'aguante', not 'aguanta'.

target: A Henri le preocupa que el invierno sea duro para sus abejas.
english: Henri worries the winter will be hard on his bees.
grammar: After 'le preocupa que' comes a worry, not a fact, so the verb turns to 'sea', not 'es'.

target: Necesito una receta que no lleve harina, viene a cenar alguien que no la puede comer.
english: I need a recipe with no flour in it – someone who can't eat it is coming round for dinner.
grammar: 'Que no lleve harina' – the recipe is still a wish, not a found thing, so its description goes subjunctive.

target: Busco un café que no sea tan amargo. ¿Cuál me sugiere?
english: I'm looking for a coffee that isn't too bitter – which would you suggest?
grammar: Hunting for something that may not exist takes the subjunctive: 'un café que no sea tan amargo'.

target: Les sugiero que lleven algo impermeable, por acá el tiempo cambia sin avisar.
english: I'd suggest you bring something waterproof, the weather round here changes without warning.
grammar: 'Lleven' – after 'les sugiero que', -ar verb llevar swaps to -e- endings, the present subjunctive's signature.

target: Me da pena que cierren la panadería de la esquina: el dueño es amabilísimo.
english: It's such a shame the bakery on the corner is closing – the owner is ever so kind.
grammar: 'Me da pena que cierren' – regret counts as emotion, so the closing goes subjunctive: 'cierren', not 'cierran'.

target: No importa que el mar esté picado, con que se pueda entrar caminando nos alcanza.
english: It doesn't matter if the sea's choppy, as long as we can walk in, that's enough for us.
grammar: 'No importa que' waves a fact aside, and dismissed facts go subjunctive: 'esté picado', not 'está'.

target: Prefiero que fijemos ya la próxima llamada, porque si lo dejamos en 'un día de estos' no pasa nunca.
english: I'd rather we pin down the next call now – if we leave it at 'one of these days' it never happens.
grammar: 'Prefiero que fijemos' – after a preference 'que' hands the verb to the subjunctive: a steered outcome, not a fact.

target: No creo que haga falta traer nada, pero por si acaso voy a llevar algo de tomar.
english: I don't think we need to bring anything, but I'll take something to drink just in case.
grammar: 'No creo que haga falta' – doubt withdraws certainty, so the subjunctive 'haga' replaces plain 'hace'.

target: Dudo que esté abierto hoy. Aquí los feriados se toman muy en serio.
english: I doubt it'll be open today – public holidays are taken very seriously here.
grammar: Doubt calls the subjunctive: 'dudo que esté abierto' – stating it as fact would keep the plain 'está'.

target: Anna se encarga de que el concurso de flores de Newbury salga bien.
english: Anna makes sure the Newbury flower contest runs smoothly.
grammar: 'Se encarga de que' aims at an outcome, not a fact, so the verb shifts: 'salga', not 'sale'.

target: Que no me aprieten estos zapatos después de una hora caminando, en la tienda se sentían comodísimos.
english: Let's just hope these shoes don't pinch after an hour's walking – in the shop they felt so comfortable.
grammar: 'Que no me aprieten' – starting a sentence with just 'que' makes it a wish: let's hope they don't pinch.

target: Mi instructora insiste en que relaje las manos y deje de tirar de las riendas.
english: My instructor insists I relax my hands and stop pulling on the reins.
grammar: 'Insiste en que' pushes for an action, so the subjunctive follows: 'relaje', not the indicative 'relajo'.

target: Es mejor que compremos los globos de una vez, mañana esas tiendas se llenan.
english: We'd better buy the balloons straight away – tomorrow those shops get packed.
grammar: 'Es mejor que compremos' – a judgement about what should happen sends the verb subjunctive: 'compremos'.

target: Les aconsejo que no manejen de noche por esa carretera, hay tramos sin señalizar.
english: I'd advise you not to drive that road at night, there are stretches with no markings at all.
grammar: 'Que no manejen' – advising against something still triggers subjunctive, the 'no' simply sits before 'manejen'.

target: Es natural que los coleccionistas quieran comprar a Brannagh. También es inútil.
english: It's natural that collectors want to buy Brannagh. It's also futile.
grammar: 'Es natural que' is a judgement, not a report – so the wanting turns subjunctive: 'quieran', not 'quieren'.

target: Dudo que exista en el mundo una ciudad más elegante que Swansea.
english: I doubt there exists a more elegant city in the world than Swansea.
grammar: 'Dudo que' casts doubt, so the verb goes subjunctive – 'exista', not 'existe'.

target: No hay vuelo directo que te lleve desde Londres a Reunión.
english: There's no direct flight to take you from London to Réunion.
grammar: The flight after 'no hay' doesn't exist, so describing it takes 'que te lleve', not 'lleva'.

target: ¿Me recomienda algún sendero que no sea muy exigente? Las rodillas ya no me acompañan como antes.
english: Could you recommend a path that isn't too demanding? My knees aren't what they were.
grammar: 'Que no sea' – the path is hoped-for, not yet identified, so its clause takes subjunctive 'sea', not 'es'.

target: No es que dudemos de su carácter, es que preferimos que ni sepa que GTA VI existe.
english: It's not that we doubt his character, we'd just rather he didn't even know GTA VI exists.
grammar: 'No es que dudemos' – 'no es que' denies an explanation, and denial pushes the verb into subjunctive.

target: Hay que amasar bien el barro para que no queden burbujas de aire.
english: You have to knead the clay properly so there are no air bubbles left in it.
grammar: 'Para que no queden' – 'para que' always takes the subjunctive: the bubble-free clay is an aim, not yet a fact.

target: Aunque lleguen tarde, no se preocupen: les dejamos la puerta de atrás sin llave.
english: Even if you get in late, don't worry – we'll leave the back door unlocked for you.
grammar: 'Aunque lleguen' – the subjunctive after 'aunque' marks a mere possibility: the late arrival may never happen.

target: Mejor no compremos más fruta hasta que se acabe la que está en el frutero.
english: Let's not buy any more fruit until we've finished what's in the bowl.
grammar: 'Hasta que se acabe' – waiting on something yet to happen, so after 'hasta que' the verb turns subjunctive.

target: Mañana nadaremos aunque llueva. Total, ya vamos a estar mojadas.
english: We'll swim tomorrow even if it rains – we'll be wet anyway.
grammar: 'Aunque llueva' – rain still up in the air takes the subjunctive: even if it rains, not even though.

target: Le dejo la receta para que me la tengan lista cuando vuelva.
english: I'll leave you the prescription so you can have it ready for when I come back.
grammar: 'Cuando vuelva' – the return is still to come, so subjunctive. A routine would take plain 'cuando vuelvo'.

target: Propongo que nadie opine sin que cite al menos una página.
english: I propose nobody gives an opinion without citing at least one page.
grammar: 'Sin que cite' – after 'sin que' (without) it's 'cite', not 'cita': the citing is the thing not happening.

target: Acerque un poco la cámara para que se vea el documento completo.
english: Move the camera in a little so the whole document is in view.
grammar: 'Para que se vea' – after 'para que' Spanish never uses the plain form: the seeing is intended, not achieved.

target: Por muy linda que sea la playa, no vale la pena manejar cinco horas para pasar un solo día.
english: However lovely the beach is, it's not worth driving five hours to spend a single day there.
grammar: 'Por muy linda que sea' – however lovely the beach may be: that open-ended may is why it's 'sea', not 'es'.

target: Anota la contraseña nueva en cuanto la cambies, para que no tengas que repetir todo el trámite.
english: Write the new password down as soon as you change it, so you don't have to go through the whole rigmarole again.
grammar: 'En cuanto la cambies' – an as-soon-as pointing at the future takes the subjunctive 'cambies', not 'cambias'.

target: Guarda el archivo antes de que la computadora se apague sola, mira que la batería está en rojo.
english: Save the file before the computer shuts itself down – look, the battery's in the red.
grammar: 'Se apague' – after 'antes de que' the verb goes subjunctive: the shutdown is a threat, not yet a fact.

target: Quien visite West Sussex en mayo verá los campos amarillos de colza.
english: Anyone visiting West Sussex in May will see the yellow rapeseed fields.
grammar: 'Quien visite' – whoever visits, nobody in particular, so the verb is 'visite' rather than everyday 'visita'.

target: Asentimos educadamente para que Gilles no arranque con otro de sus temas.
english: We nod politely so Gilles doesn't launch into another of his topics.
grammar: 'Para que Gilles no arranque' – nodding so that he won't start: after 'para que' it's 'arranque', not 'arranca'.

target: Los vecinos me dejaron sus llaves para que les riegue las plantas mientras andan de viaje.
english: The neighbours left me their keys so I can water their plants while they're away travelling.
grammar: Purpose needs the subjunctive: 'para que les riegue las plantas' – an aim rather than a fact.

target: Cuando ustedes tengan un fin de semana libre, armamos una llamada larga con todos.
english: When you've got a free weekend, we'll set up a proper long call with everyone.
grammar: 'Cuando ustedes tengan' – a 'cuando' aimed at the future takes the subjunctive: the free weekend isn't real yet.

target: Por más cuidado que tenga, siempre se me quiebra alguna pieza al desmoldarla.
english: However careful I am, I always break the odd piece getting it out of the mould.
grammar: 'Por más cuidado que tenga' – the however-much frame por más... que takes the subjunctive: 'tenga', not 'tiene'.

target: Voy a dejar pagada la cuenta esta noche para que mañana salgamos sin apuro.
english: I'll settle the bill tonight so that we can leave without a rush in the morning.
grammar: 'Para que' introduces a purpose, and purposes take the subjunctive: 'salgamos', never plain 'salimos'.

target: Cuando sea grande, Twig defenderá las instituciones democráticas.
english: When he's grown, Twig will defend democratic institutions.
grammar: 'Cuando sea grande' – a 'cuando' aimed at the future takes the subjunctive: the growing up is still ahead.

target: Dejamos los termos preparados junto a la ropa, para que nadie pierda tiempo buscando el suyo al salir.
english: We leave the flasks ready next to our clothes so nobody wastes time hunting for theirs when they come out.
grammar: 'Pierda' – after 'para que' the ending changes, but the ie from 'pierde' stays put: 'pierda', not 'perda'.

target: Encantada de conocerte. Ojalá coincidamos otra vez antes de que me vaya.
english: Lovely to meet you – I hope we run into each other again before I leave.
grammar: 'Ojalá coincidamos' – 'ojalá' (from Arabic, God-willing) always takes the subjunctive: a hope, never a fact.

target: Lord Egremont es sapientísimo y espero con ansias lo que vaya a decir.
english: Lord Egremont is most wise, and I eagerly await whatever he is going to say.
grammar: 'Sapientísimo' – the '-ísimo' ending cranks an adjective to its max: supremely wise.

target: Dejo el cuadro vuelto hacia la pared unos días para que, cuando lo mire de nuevo, salten a la vista los errores.
english: I turn the painting to face the wall for a few days, so that when I look at it again the mistakes jump straight out.
grammar: 'Cuando lo mire de nuevo' – that second look is still to come, so it's 'mire', not the everyday 'miro'.

target: Avísame apenas sepas a qué hora llega el bus, para organizarme.
english: Let me know the moment you find out what time the bus gets in, so I can sort myself out.
grammar: 'Apenas sepas' – the finding-out is still ahead, so the time connector takes subjunctive, not 'sabes'.

target: No dejan subir a la torre del reloj sin que uno vaya con guía, los escalones son muy angostos.
english: They don't let you go up the clock tower unless you're with a guide – the steps are very narrow.
grammar: 'Sin que uno vaya' – 'sin que' always takes the subjunctive: the guideless visit it names never happens.

target: Apunta los huevos en la lista antes de que se nos vuelvan a olvidar.
english: Put eggs on the list before we forget them yet again.
grammar: 'Antes de que' always takes subjunctive – so 'vuelvan', even for a forgetting that keeps on happening.

target: Envuélvamelo bien para que no se aplaste en el bolso.
english: Wrap it up well for me so it doesn't get squashed in my bag.
grammar: 'Para que' always takes the subjunctive – 'no se aplaste' states the goal, not a fact.

target: Pierre revisa cada recibo antes de que el banco alcance a equivocarse.
english: Pierre checks every receipt before the bank even gets a chance to make a mistake.
grammar: 'Antes de que el banco alcance' – what follows 'antes de que' hasn't happened yet, so 'alcance', not 'alcanza'.

target: ¿Me avisa cuando lleguemos a la plaza? No conozco bien esta ruta.
english: Will you let me know when we reach the square? I don't know this route well.
grammar: The arrival is still ahead, so it's 'cuando lleguemos' – 'llegamos' would make it a habit.

target: Guarda la dirección en el celular, no vaya a ser que nos perdamos.
english: Save the address on your phone, just in case we get lost.
grammar: 'No vaya a ser que nos perdamos' – the set phrase for just in case: it names the mishap you're trying to avoid.

target: El museo de Newbury es chiquito, pero vale la pena aunque sea por las salas de historia local.
english: The Newbury museum is tiny, but it's worth it, even if just for the local history rooms.
grammar: 'Aunque sea por las salas' – even if just for the rooms: an imagined reason, so 'sea' rather than 'es'.

target: Deja el vestido colgado en el baño mientras te bañas, para que el vapor le quite las arrugas.
english: Leave the dress hanging in the bathroom while you shower, so the steam takes the creases out.
grammar: 'Mientras te bañas' stays in the plain present – 'mientras' takes the indicative when the action is real, not future.

target: Salimos temprano para que los caballos no pasen calor en la subida.
english: We set off early so the horses don't get too hot on the climb.
grammar: A purpose is not yet a fact, so 'para que' takes the subjunctive: 'que los caballos no pasen calor'.

target: Lo voy a apuntar en el celular antes de que se me olvide cómo se escribe.
english: I'm going to note it down on my phone before I forget how it's spelled.
grammar: 'Antes de que se me olvide' – 'antes de que' always takes the subjunctive: the forgetting hasn't happened yet.

target: Por más que ofrezcan los saudíes, Brannagh no se vende.
english: However much the Saudis offer, Brannagh is not for sale.
grammar: However much is 'por más que' + subjunctive: 'ofrezcan' – the offering is open-ended, not a counted fact.

target: Te mando la foto en cuanto tenga wifi. Con estos datos no me alcanza.
english: I'll send you the photo as soon as I've got wifi – my data won't stretch to it.
grammar: 'En cuanto tenga wifi' – 'en cuanto' pointing at the future takes the subjunctive: the wifi isn't real yet.

target: Aunque el pronóstico anuncie mal tiempo, el ferry casi nunca se cancela.
english: Even if the forecast says bad weather, the ferry hardly ever gets cancelled.
grammar: 'Aunque el pronóstico anuncie' – 'anuncie' means even if it does: a forecast taken as fact would use 'anuncia'.

target: Aunque nos dé trabajo extra, a los dos nos gusta la idea de que la casa tenga un poco más de vida.
english: Even if it means extra work, we both like the idea of the house getting a bit more life.
grammar: 'Aunque nos dé' – the subjunctive after 'aunque' treats the extra work as a possibility, not an established fact.

target: Conecta el altavoz al celular para que la música se escuche hasta el fondo del patio.
english: Connect the speaker to your phone so the music carries right to the end of the patio.
grammar: 'Para que la música se escuche' – a purpose is an aim, not a fact, so its verb takes subjunctive 'escuche'.

target: Enjuaga el arroz hasta que el agua salga clara, no te toma ni dos minutos.
english: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear – it doesn't even take you two minutes.
grammar: 'Hasta que el agua salga' – the clear water is still ahead, so after 'hasta que' the verb goes subjunctive: 'salga'.

target: Deja reposar la carne unos minutos para que no pierda el jugo cuando la cortes.
english: Let the meat rest for a few minutes so it doesn't lose its juices when you cut into it.
grammar: 'Para que no pierda' – the aim isn't a fact yet, so after 'para que' the verb is 'pierda', not 'pierde'.

target: Es importante pasear a Twig temprano para que no se queme las patas.
english: It's important to walk Twig early so he doesn't burn his paws.
grammar: After 'para que', -ar verbs flip their ending to e: 'no se queme las patas', not 'se quema'.

target: En temporada de lluvias conviene salir temprano, antes de que caiga la tormenta de la tarde.
english: In the rainy season it's best to head out early, before the afternoon storm hits.
grammar: 'Antes de que caiga la tormenta' – the storm is still ahead, so after 'antes de que' it's 'caiga', not 'cae'.

target: Monto a caballo dos veces por semana, llueva o truene.
english: I ride twice a week, rain or shine.
grammar: Rain or shine is 'llueva o truene' – both verbs subjunctive: whatever the sky may do.

target: Ni se te ocurra apagar la computadora hasta que termine la actualización, aunque tarde media hora.
english: Don't even think about switching the computer off until the update finishes, even if it takes half an hour.
grammar: 'Hasta que termine' – the update's end is still pending, so 'termine' goes subjunctive, not 'termina'.

target: Ahora contamos el dinero del banco antes de que Benoît lo reparta.
english: We count the bank's money now before Benoît deals it out.
grammar: 'Antes de que' always takes the subjunctive – 'lo reparta', because the dealing hasn't happened yet.

target: Brannagh, aunque sea una yegua, me recuerda a Scout.
english: Brannagh, even though she's a horse, reminds me of Scout.
grammar: 'Aunque sea una yegua' – 'sea', not 'es': the horse part is waved aside as beside the point.

target: Aunque no entendamos ni la mitad, siempre terminamos viendo la película que propone Antoine.
english: Even if we don't understand half of it, we always end up watching whatever film Antoine suggests.
grammar: 'Aunque no entendamos' – the subjunctive turns 'aunque' from although into even if: understanding is beside the point.

target: Hoy estoy agotada. En cuanto termine la cena, me voy derecho a la cama.
english: I'm worn out today – as soon as dinner's over, I'm heading straight to bed.
grammar: A future as-soon-as goes subjunctive: 'en cuanto termine la cena' – dinner hasn't ended yet.

target: Cuando termine con el jardín, te ayudo a barrer las hojas.
english: When I'm done with the garden, I'll help you sweep up the leaves.
grammar: A future 'cuando' takes the subjunctive: 'cuando termine con el jardín' – the finishing is still ahead.

target: ¿Nos trae otra jarrita de agua cuando pueda? No hay apuro.
english: Could you bring us another jug of water when you get a chance? No rush.
grammar: 'Cuando pueda' points at an open future moment, so it takes the subjunctive – 'puede' would state a fact.

target: Guarde el pan en una bolsa de tela para que no se endurezca tan rápido.
english: Keep the bread in a cloth bag so that it doesn't go hard so quickly.
grammar: 'Para que no se endurezca' – 'para que' always takes the subjunctive: going hard is an outcome to prevent, not a fact.

target: ¿Aceptan tarjeta, o saco efectivo antes de que cierre el banco?
english: Do you take card, or shall I get cash out before the bank closes?
grammar: 'Antes de que' always triggers the subjunctive – 'cierre', since the closing is still ahead.

target: Antes de que termine el mes hay que pagar el agua y la luz, si no te cobran recargo.
english: The water and electricity have to be paid before the month is out, otherwise they add a surcharge.
grammar: 'Antes de que termine' – 'antes de que' always takes subjunctive: the month's end hasn't happened yet.

target: Voy a guardar la tarjeta de embarque en el celular, a menos que exijan la versión impresa.
english: I'll keep the boarding pass on my phone, unless they insist on a printed copy.
grammar: 'A menos que' (unless) always takes the subjunctive: 'exijan', not 'exigen' – the demand may never come.

target: Guardo cada factura numerada para que, cuando llegue la declaración de impuestos, no haya sorpresas.
english: I keep every invoice numbered so that when the tax return comes around there are no surprises.
grammar: 'Cuando llegue' – a 'cuando' pointing at the future takes the subjunctive: the tax return hasn't arrived yet.

target: Aunque salga el sol, en el altiplano refresca apenas cae la tarde.
english: Even if the sun comes out, it gets chilly on the high plateau as soon as evening falls.
grammar: 'Aunque salga el sol' – the subjunctive after 'aunque' means even if it does, not even though it did.

target: El grupo de la mañana sería el doble de grande si el agua no estuviera tan helada en invierno.
english: The morning group would be twice the size if the water weren't so freezing in winter.
grammar: 'No estuviera' – the 'si' half can trail the sentence and still takes imperfect subjunctive, paired with 'sería'.

target: Si me quedara más cerca la verdulería, compraría fresco todos los días en vez de hacer una sola compra enorme.
english: If the greengrocer's were nearer, I'd buy fresh every day instead of doing one enormous shop.
grammar: After 'si', an unreal condition takes the imperfect subjunctive 'quedara', and 'compraría' gives the result.

target: Si la señal no fuera tan mala, la videollamada no se cortaría a cada rato.
english: If the signal weren't so bad, the video call wouldn't keep dropping.
grammar: 'Si la señal no fuera tan mala' – an if that isn't true takes the imperfect subjunctive, 'cortaría' the result.

target: Si tuviera que darte un solo consejo de traducción, sería que leyeras el texto entero antes de empezar.
english: If I had to give you just one piece of translation advice, it would be to read the whole text before you start.
grammar: 'Sería que leyeras' – the unreal frame set by 'si tuviera' carries on, keeping even the advice in past subjunctive.

target: Bear no camina: se lanza en zigzag como si esquivara balas invisibles.
english: Bear doesn't walk – he hurls himself around in zigzags as if dodging invisible bullets.
grammar: 'Como si esquivara' – 'como si' always drags in the imperfect subjunctive, since the comparison is unreal.

target: Si de verdad hubieran leído el capítulo tres, no estarían tan tranquilos.
english: If they'd really read chapter three, they wouldn't look so relaxed.
grammar: After 'si', 'hubieran leído' paints the unreal past – the present result stays conditional: 'no estarían'.

target: Si el mar estuviera así de bravo todos los días, más de una se pasaría a la piscina del pueblo.
english: If the sea were this rough every day, one or two of us would give in and go to the local pool.
grammar: After 'si' the verb is 'estuviera', never 'estaría' – the would part, 'se pasaría', lives in the other half.

target: Si aquel día no hubiera llovido tanto, habríamos visto el desfile completo.
english: If it hadn't rained so much that day, we'd have seen the whole parade.
grammar: 'No hubiera llovido' imagines the rain away after the fact – 'habríamos visto' is the parade we missed.

target: Si le quedara una mesa junto a la ventana, se lo agradecería muchísimo.
english: If you had a table left by the window, I'd be terribly grateful.
grammar: 'Si le quedara' softens the ask to if you happened to have – the polite, long-shot imperfect subjunctive.

target: No me esperaba que el desierto fuera tan frío de noche. Por suerte traje un buen abrigo.
english: I wasn't expecting the desert to be so cold at night – luckily I brought a proper coat.
grammar: The past trigger 'no me esperaba' pulls what follows into the imperfect subjunctive: 'que el desierto fuera'.

target: El farmacéutico me recomendó que tomara la mitad de la dosis los primeros días.
english: The pharmacist recommended I take half the dose for the first few days.
grammar: 'Recomendó que tomara' – a past-tense trigger pulls the subjunctive into the past: 'tomara' matches 'recomendó'.

target: Si hubiéramos sabido que la obra duraba tres horas, habríamos cenado antes de entrar.
english: If we'd known the play lasted three hours, we'd have had dinner before going in.
grammar: 'Si hubiéramos sabido' – if we had known, but we didn't: the missed result follows as 'habríamos cenado'.

target: Si fuera un poquito menos tímida, conversaría con medio mundo, como hace usted.
english: If I were a little less shy, I'd chat to everyone I met – like you do.
grammar: 'Si fuera' – the unreal-if pattern: imperfect subjunctive in the if-half, conditional 'conversaría' in the answer.

target: Con el cronómetro en la mesa, los chicos terminaban el plato antes de que sonara.
english: With the timer on the table, the boys would finish their plate before it went off.
grammar: 'Antes de que' always takes the subjunctive, and in the past that's 'sonara' – the ring hadn't happened yet.

target: Si yo fuera tú, no me preocuparía tanto por el acento, lo importante es que te entiendan.
